Chlorophyll Sweeper.description:
• Venusaur, due to its ability in Chlorophyll and excellent coverage, is a strong offensive threat in the metagame. These traits are complemented by Venusaur's access to Sleep Powder, which lets it put threats it and its partners struggle with like Garchomp and Aerodactyl to sleep.

  • Earth Power versus Grass-type Coverage: Earth Power deals with Steel-types like Archaludon and Kingambit that resist its STAB moves. This coverage pairs well with its best partner in Mega Charizard Y, as Earth Power also deals with Rock- and Fire-types that Mega Charizard Y struggles to deal with, such as Glimmora and Blaziken. However, if the rest of the team is able to handle these threats, Grass-type coverage may be used instead.

  • Sleep Powder versus Grass-type coverage: Sleep Powder has shaky accuracy but makes Venusaur especially terrifying. This is because Venusaur's boosted Speed under the sun lets it shut down checks like Mega Staraptor and Incineroar. If Venusaur is using Life Orb, a third move in Solar Beam or Leaf Storm is preferred to take advantage of the damage boost.

  • Solar Beam versus Leaf Storm: Solar Beam gives Venusaur a more spammable STAB move. When boosted by Helping Hand, Solar Beam OHKOes Garchomp and Mega Aerodactyl. On the other hand, Leaf Storm OHKOes threats like Milotic regardless of the weather at the cost of dropping Venusaur's Special Attack.

  • Abilities: Chlorophyll boosts Venusaur's Speed under the sun, letting it outspeed Choice Scarf Garchomp and Hydreigon, Sneasler, and Mega Aerodactyl and put these threats to sleep or heavily damage them.

  • Items: Focus Sash makes Sleep Powder's inaccuracy easier to handle, as it lets Venusaur at least have another chance to put a foe to sleep in case it misses. Focus Sash can also be crucial to let Venusaur deal some damage or inflict sleep in case the opponent sets up Tailwind. Alternatively, Life Orb boosts Venusaur's damage, letting it take out most Pelipper with Leaf Storm and non-bulky Mega Floette with Sludge Bomb.

Other Options

  • Protect versus a Third Attacking Move: Protect may be dropped in favor of a third attacking move to maximize Venusaur's offensive capabilities, as Venusaur will generally go first under the sun and put an opposing threat to sleep or finish it off before it can attack. Furthermore, Venusaur has decent bulk, surviving hits from Kingambit, Archaludon, Garchomp, and can have extra insurance if it's using a Focus Sash. However, dropping Protect leaves it vulnerable to Fake Out disruption.

  • Energy Ball: Energy Ball is not dependent on the weather and does not drop Venusaur's Special Attack while still doing enough damage to remove Choice Scarf Basculegion-M and Mega Swampert. However, this leaves Venusaur unable to OHKO bulky Basculegion-M.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: While Venusaur can invalidate most of its offensive checks with Sleep Powder, it can find itself in an extremely bad situation if Sleep Powder misses. Venusaur also fails to OHKO most threats like Mega Staraptor, Mega Metagross, and Hydreigon even with the Life Orb boost and will get OHKOed back.

  • Bulkier Steel- and Grass-types like Gholdengo and Mega Venusaur give problems to Venusaur, as they shrug off its attacks. If Venusaur is lacking Earth Power, Gholdengo can even use it as setup fodder and OHKO it with +2 Make it Rain.

  • Weather setters like Alolan Ninetales, Mega Tyranitar, and Pelipper can swap in and shut down Venusaur's ability, allowing their teammates to outspeed and remove it.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Charizard Y is Venusaur's best partner, as it sets sun to activate Chlorophyll and deals with Steel- and Grass-types that Venusaur struggles with, such as Gholdengo, Sinistcha, and Mega Venusaur.

  • Tailwind setters such as Aerodactyl and Whimsicott provide an extra Speed boost to match opposing teams' Tailwind. Aerodactyl also deals with opposing Mega Charizard Y and Mega Delphox, while Whimsicott provides more disruption in Encore and can also use Fake Tears to allow Venusaur to pick up surprise OHKOs.

  • Incineroar helps Venusaur put a foe to sleep more safely by using Fake Out, and it also deals with Mega Metagross and Gholdengo.

  • An alternative sun setter in Torkoal may be considered, as it frees up the Mega Evolution slot and allows the rest of the team to utilize other modes of play, such as Trick Room. Torkoal also provides Helping Hand support, which allows Venusaur to OHKO Archaludon, Mega Metagross, and Garchomp.

Bulky Attacker.description:
• Mega Venusaur is a solid option thanks to its bulk, good coverage, and excellent matchup against Basculegion-M, Sylveon, Rotom-Wash, and Mega Floette. It also has a decent matchup against many common threats, such as Sneasler, Kingambit, and Incineroar.

  • Earth Power: Earth Power provides coverage against Steel- and Poison-types that Mega Venusaur would otherwise be unable to damage. Examples include Kingambit, Sneasler, Archaludon, and Mega Gengar, all of which Mega Venusaur can 2HKO. It also notably 3HKOes Incineroar, which Mega Venusaur can beat thanks to Thick Fat.

  • Mega Evolving Venusaur: When in the sun, Venusaur can outspeed the entire unboosted metagame. This means it may not always be optimal to Mega Evolve Venusaur when facing foes like Mega Charizard Y, as remaining in its base forme allows it to use an extremely fast Sleep Powder or clean up a weakened foe before it can attack. Alternatively, Mega Evolution provides Mega Venusaur with Thick Fat, which turns Mega Dragonite's Flamethrower from a 2HKO into a 4HKO, Mega Froslass's Blizzard from a 2HKO into a 3HKO, and Mega Charizard Y's Weather Ball in the sun from a guaranteed OHKO into a 2HKO.

Other Options

  • Leech Seed: Leech Seed lets Mega Venusaur deal residual damage and increase its longevity. It helps Mega Venusaur win in the long term against bulky foes like Corviknight, which it otherwise can't damage well. Leech Seed will usually replace Earth Power or Giga Drain due to the importance of Sludge Bomb and Protect. Without Earth Power, Mega Venusaur lacks meaningful damage against Steel- and Poison-types like Kingambit and Sneasler. Without Giga Drain, Mega Venusaur becomes far less threatening to Water-types like Basculegion-M.

  • Sleep Powder: Sleep Powder can end a game if it hits, and Venusaur can use it multiple times in a single game thanks to its amazing bulk. However, Sleep Powder also comes at the cost of a precious move slot, meaning it will most likely replace Earth Power or Giga Drain. It can also make Venusaur a more inconsistent Pokemon to bring due to its poor accuracy.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 7 Def / 18 SpA / 9 Spe with Modest: This spread allows Venusaur to outspeed Choice Scarf Basculegion-M in the sun. The HP and Defense investment allows Venusaur to survive +2 Black Glasses Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave. The remaining SPs are invested in Special Attack to maximize damage, allowing Mega Venusaur to still 2HKO specially defensive Archaludon sets.

  • 32 HP / 19 Def / 12 SpD / 3 Spe with Bold: 3 Speed SPs allow Venusaur to outspeed Mega Delphox in the sun. The remaining SPs are invested in bulk, allowing Venusaur to comfortably survive Psychic from Modest Mega Delphox, Brave Bird from Talonflame, and even a 200-Base Power Last Respects from Adamant Choice Scarf Adaptability Basculegion-M.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Although Mega Venusaur is protected from its usual weaknesses through Thick Fat, it is still weak to Flying- and Psychic-type attacks. This includes Pelipper, Mega Aerodactyl, Talonflame, Farigiraf, and Mega Delphox. Mega Delphox and Talonflame are particularly big problems, as they resist Giga Drain, are immune to Earth Power, and threaten it back with Psychic and Brave Bird, respectively. Mega Dragonite can also tank any attack from Mega Venusaur and 3HKO it with Dragon Pulse. It can also set up Tailwind right in front of Mega Venusaur. Corviknight completely walls Mega Venusaur; it can easily set up in front of Mega Venusaur and KO it with Brave Bird.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Rain teams appreciate Mega Venusaur's ability to switch into Grass-, Fighting-, and Electric-type attacks such as Sneasler's Close Combat and Rotom-Wash's Thunderbolt for partners like Archaludon, Pelipper, and Basculegion-M. It can also use Earth Power against Kingambit for Basculegion-M. In return, Archaludon can use Electro Shot to deal with Flying-types like Corviknight and Talonflame, while Basculegion-M can take out Mega Delphox. Pelipper can also switch in and massively reduce Mega Charizard Y's damage to Mega Venusaur with Drizzle. Kingambit and Incineroar are decent switch-ins to Psychic-type moves. They help check Farigiraf, which can easily tank Mega Venusaur's attacks and 2HKO it, while Mega Venusaur can switch into Fighting-type moves for them. Sableye is also a good switch-in to Psychic-type moves, as it can set up screens to make Mega Venusaur even harder to remove. In return, Mega Venusaur can handle the Fairy-types that threaten Sableye.

  • How to Overcome Mega Venusaur's Weaknesses: Pelipper, Archaludon, and Basculegion-M are great partners to bring against weather teams, as Pelipper hampers Mega Charizard Y's Weather Ball and shuts down Mega Froslass's Aurora Veil, while Archaludon and Basculegion-M threaten them with Electro Shot and Last Respects. Partners like Sableye are better against setup spam and hyper offense teams; Sableye can use Encore to lock Mega Blastoise into Shell Smash while providing priority screens. Knowing when to use Protect is also very important for positioning, as it gives the team an extra turn to bring in Basculegion-M to threaten Psychic- and Fire-types, Pelipper against Mega Charizard Y, or Sableye to set up screens and shield Mega Venusaur from a strong attack.

Sun Sweeper.description:
• Mega Charizard Y is a ruthless sweeper dealing immense damage with its Fire-type attacks. It threatens OHKOs and 2HKOs on the majority of the metagame such as Mega Floette, Kingambit, Sinistcha, and Mega Metagross. Mega Charizard Y opts to run bulk rather than maximizing its offense and Speed to help it survive longer in contrast to Regulation M-A.

  • Three Attacks Sweeper: Mega Charizard Y dominates simply using three attacks: Heat Wave, Weather Ball, and Solar Beam. Heat Wave provides powerful spread Fire-type damage. Weather Ball deals insane Fire-type damage while sun is active or provides handy coverage depending on the weather, and it is unaffected by Wide Guard. Solar Beam is necessary to threaten Water-types like Basculegion-M and Mega Swampert.

  • Drought: The sun set by Drought increases the damage of Mega Charizard Y's Fire-type attacks, guaranteeing that Heat Wave will OHKO Kingambit and Sinistcha. It also allows Solar Beam to be used in a single turn, enables Venusaur's Chlorophyll, and reduces the damage of Wave Crash from Basculegion-M and Mega Swampert.

  • Mega Evolving Charizard: Mega Charizard Y should not Mega Evolve right away unless there are no foes that can override the sun. It is best to wait until the opponent has sent out or Mega Evolved their weather setter like Pelipper and Mega Froslass before Mega Evolving Mega Charizard Y to ensure sun is not overridden.

Other Options

  • Helping Hand: Helping Hand can be run over Solar Beam when Mega Charizard Y is paired with Venusaur. Helping Hand-boosted Solar Beam from Life Orb Venusaur OHKOs Garchomp and Mega Aerodactyl, dealing significantly more damage than Mega Charizard Y's own Solar Beam.

  • Ancient Power: Ancient Power is a niche move used instead of Solar Beam primarily as a surprise attack to OHKO opposing Mega Charizard Y and to let it threaten Ceruledge and Hisuian Arcanine. An omni boost from Ancient Power is also extremely beneficial for Mega Charizard Y, letting it survive Rock Slide and giving it a chance to OHKO Mega Floette with Weather Ball.

SP Spreads

  • 16 HP / 25 Def / 12 SpA / 13 Spe with Modest: The given spread lets Mega Charizard Y survive Rock Slide from non-Life Orb Garchomp and gives it a good chance to survive Mystic Water-boosted Wave Crash from Adaptability Jolly Basculegion-M in the sun. 13 Speed SPs let Mega Charizard Y outspeed maximum Speed Modest Venusaur without active Chlorophyll, and the remaining SPs are invested into Special Attack to maximize Mega Charizard Y's damage output.

  • 30 HP / 31 Def / 1 SpA / 4 Spe with Modest: This bulkier SP spread provides Mega Charizard Y with a high chance to survive Rock Slide from Life Orb-boosted Jolly Garchomp and Aerodactyl and grants a favorable chance to survive Wave Crash from Life Orb-boosted Adaptability Basculegion-M in the sun. The Speed investment ensures Mega Charizard Y outruns Adamant Mega Swampert and Mega Tyranitar in the sun, and the remaining SPs are put into Special Attack.

  • 16 HP / 17 Def / 10 SpA / 23 Spe with Timid: This faster SP spread allows Mega Charizard Y to outspeed Excadrill in the sun as well as Glimmora and Hisuian Arcanine. The defensive investment allows Mega Charizard Y to survive Rock Slide from -1 Lycanroc-D, and the leftover SPs maximize Mega Charizard Y's Special Attack.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Mega Charizard Y's biggest adversaries are Rock-types such as Mega Tyranitar, Mega Aerodactyl, Lycanroc-D, and Glimmora. They all easily threaten OHKOs with Rock Slide, Accelerock, and Power Gem respectively while Mega Charizard Y struggles to KO them.

  • Mega Raichu Y outspeeds Mega Charizard Y and easily threatens an OHKO with Zap Cannon.

  • Rain teams are difficult for Mega Charizard Y to defeat. Rain significantly reduces the damage of Heat Wave and Solar Beam, and it enables Mega Swampert's Swift Swim, allowing it to outspeed and OHKO Mega Charizard Y with Wave Crash. Pelipper, Archaludon, and Sinistcha are also difficult for Mega Charizard Y to remove while rain is active. Pelipper and Archaludon threaten to OHKO Mega Charizard Y with Weather Ball and Electro Shot, respectively. Sinistcha can also set up Trick Room, allowing Pelipper and Archaludon to attack first, and it can provide them with redirection as well as healing thanks to Hospitality.

  • Although Mega Charizard Y can survive their attacks, Garchomp and Basculegion-M are still threats to it. Mega Charizard Y is naturally outrun by Garchomp and is unable to KO it with Solar Beam before Garchomp attacks twice with Rock Slide. Basculegion-M can outspeed Mega Charizard Y with Tailwind support from Whimsicott, giving Basculegion-M an opportunity to KO Mega Charizard Y before it can attack.

  • While it is an uncommon pick, Ceruledge walls all of Mega Charizard Y's attacks, so it can easily take advantage of this to set up with Bulk Up and proceed to snowball.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Garchomp and Basculegion-M are Mega Charizard Y's best partners, easily threatening Rock-types and Ceruledge as well as opposing Garchomp and Basculegion-M. Garchomp in particular can remove Mega Raichu Y. They are also great at pressuring opposing Mega Charizard Y.

  • While Mega Floette cannot be used in the same battle as Mega Charizard Y, it synergizes well as an alternative Mega Evolution when Mega Charizard Y has an unfavorable matchup. Mega Floette is great at removing Garchomp and deals devastating damage to Pokemon commonly found on rain teams like Pelipper, Mega Swampert, and Archaludon. In return, Mega Charizard Y can easily threaten Mega Metagross, Gholdengo, Mega Gengar, and Mega Mawile, all of which Mega Floette is threatened by.

  • Incineroar is great at providing damage mitigation with Intimidate, ensuring that Mega Charizard Y survives Rock Slide from the Rock-types and Garchomp. It also provides Fake Out support to let Mega Charizard Y dish out damage safely.

  • Venusaur threatens Mega Aerodactyl and Garchomp, which Mega Charizard Y struggles to damage, as well as common Water-types like Basculegion-M, Mega Blastoise, and Mega Swampert. Sleep Powder can also disrupt foes, letting Mega Charizard Y stick around for longer.

Bulky Sweeper.description:
• Mega Charizard Y is very popular in the M-A metagame and has incredible sweeping potential due to its monstrous Special Attack stat and ability to set up sun. It can punish common Steel- and Grass-type foes such as Kingambit, Aegislash, and Sinistcha with its sun-boosted Fire-type attacks.

  • Sun-Affected Moves: Mega Charizard Y's sun helps it secure OHKOs against foes such as Kingambit, Aegislash, and Sinistcha with Heat Wave. Weather Ball takes advantage of sun by becoming another Fire-type STAB move that deals immense damage against specially defensive foes such as Mega Floette, Farigiraf, and Mega Gardevoir. Weather Ball also adapts to opposing weather, punishing foes like Maushold with a 2HKO in rain. The move can also get around Wide Guard from the likes of Aegislash and Aerodactyl. Solar Beam helps Mega Charizard Y threaten Water-type foes such as Milotic and Basculegion-M, OHKOing non-bulky Basculegion-M sets and 2HKOing Milotic and Garchomp.

  • Weather Wars: Mega Charizard Y can't always set up sun safely, as foes such as Alolan Ninetales, Mega Froslass, Pelipper, and Mega Tyranitar can change the weather upon switching in. Positioning is very important for Mega Charizard Y so that it can make full use of sun and not worry about it being overridden. Aside from switching Mega Charizard Y out, waiting to Mega Evolve is an optimal choice to prevent losing the weather war.

Abilities

Drought: Drought sets up sun, supporting partners by activating abilities like Venusaur's Chlorophyll and supporting Mega Charizard Y itself by increasing the damage of its Fire-type attacks and weakening Water-type attacks from threats like Milotic. Drought often forces opposing weather teams to remove Mega Charizard Y before executing their plans so they can maintain their weather. Drought can thwart opposing weather like rain by hindering the offensive capabilities of Swift Swim Basculegion-M and Pelipper. Mega Froslass struggles to set up Aurora Veil or rely on Blizzard in the face of Mega Charizard Y's Drought.

SP Spreads

  • 14 HP / 28 Def / 11 SpA / 13 Spe with Modest: The bulk on this spread allows Mega Charizard Y to survive Rock Slide from the likes of Excadrill and Garchomp, as well as Wave Crash from Basculegion-M as long as sun is active. The Special Attack SPs help it OHKO Basculegion-M with Solar Beam and give it a chance to OHKO Aegislash in Shield forme as well as Mega Froslass with Heat Wave. The Speed investment allows Mega Charizard Y to outspeed Adamant Swift Swim Basculegion-M while supported by Tailwind.

  • 24 HP / 14 Def / 11 SpA / 17 Spe with Modest: This spread offers more Speed than the previous spread while still giving Mega Charizard Y a good chance to survive Rock Slide from Excadrill and Garchomp, though it is not guaranteed. The HP investment allows it to avoid a 2HKO from Mega Gengar's Shadow Ball and almost always avoid a 2HKO from Rotom-Wash's Hydro Pump while in sun. The Speed helps it move before Archaludon and non-maximum Speed Rotom formes.

  • 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Timid: This spread maximizes Mega Charizard Y's Speed and Special Attack. The Speed investment helps Mega Charizard Y outspeed maximum Speed Glimmora as well as maximum Speed Rotom formes while guaranteeing at least a Speed tie with Mega Kangaskhan. The Special Attack investment allows Weather Ball to 2HKO Mega Floette in sun.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: While all Pokemon that change the weather away from sun prove to be a problem for Mega Charizard Y, it struggles most against Mega Tyranitar's sand and Pelipper's rain. Mega Tyranitar's sand enables Sand Rush Excadrill to move before Mega Charizard Y and threaten it with Rock Slide, while Mega Charizard Y struggles to deal any significant damage to Mega Tyranitar in sand and can be OHKOed by its Rock Slide in return. Pelipper's rain enables Swift Swim Basculegion-M, which threatens Mega Charizard Y with its Water-type moves. Rain can also grant Pelipper a Water-type Weather Ball, which is enough to OHKO Mega Charizard Y. Choice Scarf Garchomp and Aerodactyl can threaten Mega Charizard Y with Rock Slide, with Aerodactyl being able to OHKO it. Glimmora can easily threaten Mega Charizard Y with Power Gem and is a great pick in mirror matchups against opposing Mega Charizard Y. Opposing Glimmora and bulky Garchomp have an easier time threatening Mega Charizard Y under Tailwind.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Whimsicott can support Mega Charizard Y with Tailwind, helping it outspeed threats such as Choice Scarf Garchomp, and use Encore to put a foe into an unfavorable position, such as Sneasler after it uses Fake Out. Other Fairy-type partners like Mega Floette and Sylveon can threaten Dragon-type foes that resist Mega Charizard Y's Fire-type moves, such as Mega Dragonite and Garchomp, with Whimsicott and Sylveon not taking up a Mega slot. Aerodactyl has access to Tailwind and Wide Guard to prevent Rock Slide spam, as well Unnerve, which can help it deal with Sitrus Berry Basculegion-M and Garchomp sets. Garchomp can help against opposing Garchomp with Dragon Claw and opposing Mega Charizard Y with Rock Slide. It can also use Earthquake next to Mega Charizard Y to threaten Rock-type foes such as Mega Tyranitar, Hisuian Arcanine, and both Mega and base Glimmora. Basculegion-M is a strong sweeper that can handle opposing Fire-types such as Mega Delphox with Wave Crash or Aqua Jet, while Last Respects can be used as a general sweeping option due to its immense damage output. Kingambit helps in the Trick Room matchup due to its low Speed and can also threaten Basculegion-M with Sucker Punch and Farigiraf with Kowtow Cleave. Sneasler pairs well with Mega Charizard Y, as it provides Fake Out support and can threaten Rock-type foes such as Mega Tyranitar and Lycanroc-D with Close Combat. Incineroar also provides Fake Out and Intimidate support against foes such as Basculegion-M and Garchomp, and it can threaten Basculegion-M with Throat Chop or Darkest Lariat.

  • How to Overcome Mega Charizard Y's Weaknesses: Leading with Mega Charizard Y can be risky against opposing weather teams, as it could easily lose weather control. Keeping it in the back can help position around opposing weather set by Pelipper and Mega Tyranitar. Eliminating opposing weather setters can put Mega Charizard Y in an advantageous position, as it no longer has to worry about sun being removed. Waiting to Mega Evolve until opposing weather has already been set up can also grant it a favorable position. It does, however, struggle to damage Dragon-type foes such as Dragonite, Garchomp, and Archaludon in rain. Having a Fairy- or Dragon-type partner such as Sylveon, Mega Floette, or Garchomp can help against the aforementioned foes. Mega Floette is great at covering matchups that Mega Charizard Y struggles against, such as Mega Tyranitar and Dragonite teams. Basculegion-M can help against Rock-type threats like Mega Tyranitar, Hisuian Arcanine, and Aerodactyl with its Water-type moves. Opposing Tailwind can cause foes such as Mega Tyranitar and Glimmora to outspeed Mega Charizard Y. Whimsicott can counter opposing Tailwind with a Tailwind of its own or by using Taunt on the opposing Tailwind user. Dual screens from foes like Sableye can also cause Mega Charizard Y and its partners to lose momentum. Stalling out screen turns with Protect or switching is an option to get around them. Protect and switching around are ways to avoid Fake Out cycling aimed at Mega Charizard Y.

Setup Sweeper.description:
• Mega Blastoise uses Shell Smash and Water Spout to become a strong spread damage dealer after a supported setup turn. Mega Blastoise's natural bulk gives it setup opportunities with support from Fake Out, Rage Powder, or Armor Tail. However, it must be positioned carefully because chip damage weakens Water Spout, and Shell Smash's defense drops make it easier to revenge kill.

  • Shell Smash: After a Shell Smash boost, Mega Blastoise can outspeed most of the unboosted metagame, which makes a full-power Water Spout extremely difficult to switch around.

  • Water Spout: At full power, +2 Water Spout threatens OHKOs on offensive Garchomp, Farigiraf, Kingambit, and Sylveon, and it can even OHKO Mega Charizard Y through sun and Mega Tyranitar in sand.

  • Dark Pulse: Dark Pulse is a reliable attack to fall back on after Water Spout has been weakened, hitting Ghost- and Psychic-types such as Sinistcha, Mega Gengar, Aegislash, Basculegion-M, and Farigiraf. Notably, it has a high chance to 2HKO Basculegion-M even after Leftovers recovery. Its low flinch chance can also help against slower targets that survive the first hit, though it should not be relied on as Mega Blastoise's main way of breaking through checks.

  • Protect versus Fake Out: Protect is preferred because Mega Blastoise must respect both foes targeting it before and after it sets up, and Protect can also let Mega Blastoise stall Tailwind, weather, or Trick Room turns while its partner attacks. Fake Out is an alternative for teams that want Mega Blastoise to help create the opening turn instead. However, it is harder to justify on teams already using Sneasler or Incineroar, and losing Protect makes Mega Blastoise much easier to overwhelm after it boosts.

Other Options

  • Ice Beam: Ice Beam can be used over Shell Smash to hit Dragon- and Grass-types such as Garchomp, Mega Dragonite, and Venusaur more effectively. However, dropping Shell Smash makes Mega Blastoise much less threatening against neutral targets, especially once Water Spout has been weakened.

  • Aura Sphere: Aura Sphere can be used over Protect or Fake Out to give Mega Blastoise coverage for Kingambit, Archaludon, Hydreigon, and Mega Kangaskhan, notably always 2HKOing Archaludon. That said, losing Protect or Fake Out makes it harder for Mega Blastoise to either keep itself safe or help create its own setup turn.

SP Spreads

  • 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Modest: This spread maximizes Mega Blastoise's damage and Speed, making it the preferred option for sweeping with Shell Smash. Even before boosting, a full-power Water Spout OHKOes Mega Delphox and Mega Aerodactyl. After a Shell Smash, Mega Blastoise outspeeds fast unboosted threats such as Mega Gengar, Mega Delphox, and Sneasler, as well as Choice Scarf users such as Garchomp, Rotom-Wash, and Basculegion-M. At +2, Dark Pulse OHKOes Sinistcha and has a chance to OHKO Farigiraf, while a full-power Water Spout OHKOes specially bulky Corviknight.

  • 32 HP / 2 Def / 32 SpA with Modest: This bulkier spread keeps maximum Special Attack investment while trading Speed for better chances to set up against super effective hits. It notably lets Mega Blastoise survive Mega Charizard Y's Solar Beam and Rotom-Wash's Thunderbolt. The lack of Speed investment means Mega Blastoise misses out on outspeeding threats such as Mega Gengar, Mega Delphox, Choice Scarf Garchomp, and Choice Scarf Jolly Basculegion-M after a Shell Smash. Because of this, Mega Blastoise benefits more from Trick Room support from partners like Farigiraf and Sinistcha, since it can still use Shell Smash to boost its damage without relying as heavily on the Speed boost under Trick Room.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Mega Blastoise is heavily dependent on keeping its HP high, since chip damage, Fake Out, priority moves, and double targeting can quickly weaken Water Spout. Fake Out is especially disruptive after Mega Blastoise has already set up, as it can stop Water Spout for a turn and give the opponent time to chip Mega Blastoise, reposition, or stall out Tailwind. Priority moves such as Kingambit's Sucker Punch, Aegislash's Shadow Sneak, and Mega Dragonite's Extreme Speed are problematic, as they can deal meaningful damage with Shell Smash's defense drops and weaken Water Spout before Mega Blastoise gets to attack. Wide Guard from Pokemon such as Aerodactyl, Pelipper, and Aegislash blocks Water Spout entirely and forces Mega Blastoise to rely on single-target attacks. Pokemon like Venusaur and Rotom-Wash threaten Mega Blastoise with super effective damage. Mega Venusaur is especially difficult to break, as it comfortably takes Dark Pulse and Ice Beam while threatening Mega Blastoise with Giga Drain. Archaludon can threaten Mega Blastoise with Electro Shot in rain, but it is not always a safe answer after Mega Blastoise has boosted, as a +2 full-power Water Spout in rain can still deal massive damage to it. Dragon-types like Hydreigon and Kommo-o resist both Water Spout and Dark Pulse, with Hydreigon further weakening Mega Blastoise through Snarl. Mega Dragonite can also take a hit thanks to Multiscale and threaten back with Thunderbolt. Sun from Mega Charizard Y and Torkoal weakens Water Spout, making it harder for Mega Blastoise to brute force teams with spread damage.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Sinistcha is one of Mega Blastoise's best partners. Its Rage Powder can redirect attacks, while Hospitality and Life Dew keep Water Spout strong. Farigiraf supports Mega Blastoise with Armor Tail, blocking priority moves such as Kingambit's Sucker Punch and Fake Out from Mega Kangaskhan, Sneasler, and Incineroar. Sinistcha and Farigiraf can also set Trick Room, giving an uninvested Mega Blastoise a way to attack faster teams without needing to use Shell Smash. In return, Fake Out variants of Mega Blastoise can help them set Trick Room. Partners like Sneasler and Incineroar provide Fake Out support, helping Mega Blastoise find setup oppurtunities; they also disrupt Wide Guard users such as Aerodactyl and Pelipper for a turn to let Water Spout connect. Additionally, Sneasler threatens Kingambit, Archaludon, and Hydregion with Close Combat, while Incineroar weakens physical attackers with Intimidate and can pivot with Parting Shot. With Rage Powder and Sleep Powder, Vivillon can deny attacks directed at Mega Blastoise, and it can also use Hurricane to pressure Grass-types, which resist Water Spout. Furthermore, Vivillon's Tailwind immediately gives Mega Blastoise speed control without requiring Shell Smash; and its Rain Dance removes sun from Mega Charizard Y and Torkoal while strengthening Water Spout, allowing Mega Blastoise to OHKO uninvested Garchomp and 2HKO Sinistcha. Maushold can support Mega Blastoise with Follow Me as well as Rain Dance and Feint, with Feint being especially useful for breaking Protect and Wide Guard so that Water Spout can connect. Basculegion-M appreciates Mega Blastoise pressuring Pokemon such as Sinistcha, Farigiraf, and Aegislash with Dark Pulse. In return, it can target Mega Gardevoir's and Mega Floette's lower Defense stats while acting as another strong Water-type attacker that pressures Fire-types such as Mega Charizard Y.

  • How to Overcome Mega Blastoise's Weaknesses: Mega Blastoise should usually be positioned with a support Pokemon that either helps it preserve its HP or prevents it from being picked off after setting up. Redirection from Sinistcha, Vivillon, or Maushold can protect it from single-target attacks, while Farigiraf prevents priority moves from cutting a sweep short. Against Wide Guard users, Mega Blastoise should use Dark Pulse or Aura Sphere instead of Water Spout; partners such as Sneasler, Kingambit, and Basculegion-M can also pressure these Pokemon so that it doesn't only rely on Feint and Fake Out support. Against sun teams, avoid setting up with Mega Blastoise too early because Mega Charizard Y and Torkoal can weaken Water Spout; instead, use teammates such as Basculegion-M, Sneasler, and Incineroar to pressure them before it attempts to sweep.

Offensive Support.description:
• Alolan Ninetales utilizes its support movepool in conjunction with its ability to set snow to disrupt the common weather setters of the format like Mega Charizard Y and Mega Tyranitar while boasting strong matchups into metagame staples like Garchomp, Sinistcha, and Whimsicott.

  • Aurora Veil: Aurora Veil allows Alolan Ninetales to, in the snow, survive attacks such as Heat Wave from Modest Mega Charizard Y and Dire Claw from Adamant Sneasler and almost always survive 200 Base Power Last Respects from Adamant Adaptability Basculegion-M.

  • Encore: Encore allows Alolan Ninetales to punish defensive play from the likes of Kingambit and Mega Aerodactyl, scaring them away from setting up Swords Dance and setting Tailwind, respectively. It also heavily punishes Fake Out from Pokemon such as Incineroar and Sneasler.

Other Options

========

  • Freeze-Dry: Freeze-Dry allows Alolan Ninetales to threaten heavy damage onto Basculegion-M and Pelipper while providing an Ice-type STAB move that isn't thwarted by Wide Guard. This does come at the cost of Encore, however, weakening the utility of Alolan Ninetales.

  • Disable: Disable + Encore is a devastating duo that can easily turn foes against themselves, especially when combined with Mega Gengar, providing them with no escape. In order to run Disable, it must be used over Aurora Veil, though this doesn't particularly matter to the teams that Disable Alolan Ninetales is placed on, as they appreciate its ability to shut down foes for allies like the aforementioned Mega Gengar to set up Perish Song.

Items

========

  • Never-Melt Ice: Never-Melt Ice allows Alolan Ninetales to 2HKO low bulk variants of Sneasler a solid amount of the time and always OHKO Whimsicott with Blizzard.

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash increases Alolan Ninetales's survivability, allowing it to survive attacks such as Mega Gengar's Sludge Bomb and retaliate back or use Encore or Disable.

Abilities

========

  • Snow Warning: Snow Warning sets up the snow, allowing Alolan Ninetales to survive Wave Crash from Adamant Adaptability Choice Scarf Basculegion-M, increase Blizzard's accuracy, and use Aurora Veil.

Teambuilding

========

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Fire-type Pokemon like Incineroar and Mega Charizard Y threaten Alolan Ninetales with huge damage by using Flare Blitz and Heat Wave, respectively. Mega Charizard Y, as well as other weather setters like Mega Tyranitar, can shut off the snow, making Blizzard unreliable and rendering Aurora Veil useless. Mega Tyranitar, similar to Mega Charizard Y, also has the ability to deal big damage to Alolan Ninetales with Rock Slide. Other Rock-type Pokemon like Mega Aerodactyl and Lycanroc-D threaten Alolan Ninetales with Rock Slide, with the former being able to outspeed Alolan Ninetales or use Wide Guard to prevent it from dealing damage. Steel-type Pokemon like Kingambit and Archaludon threaten to OHKO Alolan Ninetales with Iron Head and Flash Cannon, respectively, even when the snow and Aurora Veil are set up. Sneasler and Mega Gengar can outspeed Alolan Ninetales and threaten it with Dire Claw and Sludge Bomb. Trick Room from Farigiraf enables strong attackers like Torkoal, turning Alolan Ninetales's high Speed against it and allowing them to outspeed and OHKO Alolan Ninetales with Eruption.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Garchomp threatens the Fire-, Rock-, Steel-, and Poison-type Pokemon that all threaten Alolan Ninetales with Earthquake and Stomping Tantrum while targeting down Mega Aerodactyl and Mega Charizard Y with Rock Slide. In return, Alolan Ninetales threatens opposing Garchomp and other Dragon-type Pokemon like Hydreigon and Mega Dragonite while using Encore to prevent setup sweepers like Mega Floette from getting out of hand. Kingambit can scare away opposing Trick Room by being able to take advantage of it itself and threatening Farigiraf and Sinistcha, common Trick Room setters, with Kowtow Cleave. It also scares away Incineroar thanks to Defiant and threatens Mega Tyranitar and opposing Kingambit with Low Kick, opposing Rock-type Pokemon with Iron Head, and Mega Gengar with Kowtow Cleave and Sucker Punch. Alolan Ninetales uses Aurora Veil to give Kingambit an easier time setting up and threatens Garchomp with Blizzard. Mega Gengar appreciates Encore and potentially Disable from Alolan Ninetales to shut down troublesome Pokemon for it like Kingambit and Incineroar, and it traps and KOes Pokemon like Mega Tyranitar and Archaludon in return with Perish Song. Mega Pokemon like Mega Glimmora and Mega Aerodactyl are helpful as well, using their Rock-type STAB moves to KO opposing Fire-type Pokemon.

  • How to Overcome Alolan Ninetales's Weaknesses: Using Pokemon that beat opposing weather setters is mandatory for Alolan Ninetales, as it needs the snow to be up for many of its main qualities. Consider bring Alolan Ninetales into weather matchups as well, as it can override opposing weather. When combined with Mega Gengar, opposing weather setters can stay trapped, leaving snow as the prevailing weather and making foes like Archaludon and Excadrill much less threatening.

Perish Trapper.description:
• Mega Gengar uses its Shadow Tag ability to stop foes from switching, heavily limiting the opponent's options, and its high Speed and Special Attack allow it to threaten foes like Basculegion-M and Sinistcha. Perish Song allows it to take out foes without damaging them directly, and Shadow Tag stops opponents from removing the Perishing counter by switching.

  • Perish Trap Strategy: Mega Gengar can force opponents to adopt an offensive playstyle to claim KOs before the Perishing counter runs out then punish these plays with Disable. The rest of the team can be built around disrupting foes and supporting Mega Gengar as opposed to dealing damage, though sweepers can be put on the team to force the opponent to cover for them and be used against Perish Song's poor matchups. A team can further commit to this strategy with a second Perish Song setter to keep up momentum, given that Mega Gengar will usually switch out on the last turn of Perish Song. This strategy allows you to neglect foes' defenses.

  • Disable vs. Sludge Bomb: Disable allows Mega Gengar to block detrimental moves, such as Kowtow Cleave from Kingambit and Parting Shot from Incineroar, which would otherwise let it switch out. When paired with a teammate using Encore such as Maushold or Whimsicott, it can completely shut down a foe. Sludge Bomb is an alternative that hits Fairy-types like Mega Floette and Sylveon, helping teammates like Kommo-o sweep.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 29 Def / 5 Spe with Timid: The defensive investment allows Mega Gengar to survive 100-Base Power Last Respects from Basculegion-M at -1 almost always, Psychic and Psyshock from Mega Delphox with Friend Guard active, and Earthquake from Excadrill. The Speed investment allows it to always outrun Garchomp and Mega Floette.

  • 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Timid: Mega Gengar can be played as a fast offensive Pokemon by forgoing Perish Song. It has good coverage with Shadow Ball and Sludge Bomb, and keeping Disable allows for Disable and Encore combinations, which are still useful even without a Perish Song mode. Shadow Ball is much more likely to OHKO Basculegion-M and Sinistcha with maximized Special Attack, and Sludge Bomb will deal such heavy damage to Mega Floette and Sylveon that they will faint soon if they are poisoned. The added Speed makes it easier to disrupt faster foes like Sneasler with Disable. A team built around this set should be comprised mostly of offensive Pokemon like Sneasler to cover for Mega Gengar's weakness to Dark-type Pokemon, as opposed to heavy support.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Ghost-types like Basculegion-M and opposing Mega Gengar are able to switch out despite Shadow Tag and threaten an OHKO on Mega Gengar with boosted Last Respects and Shadow Ball, respectively. Mega Delphox outspeeds it and threatens an OHKO with Psychic. Opposing Dark-types like Kingambit and Incineroar can threaten an OHKO onto Mega Gengar, and Kingambit cannot be weakened by Intimidate. Moves like Parting Shot from Incineroar and Volt Switch from Rotom-W bypass Shadow Tag, thus preventing Perish Song from getting a KO. Garchomp threatens heavy damage that cannot be redirected with Earthquake, and it pairs well with Flying-types like Mega Charizard Y and Aerodactyl, which have spread attacks of their own that can finish Mega Gengar off. Mega Charizard Y in particular can also threaten an OHKO with Weather Ball, making Mega Charizard Y and Garchomp a deadly combination. Taunt from Pokemon like Whimsicott prevents Mega Gengar from getting Perish Song off or stalling turns with Protect.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Incineroar's Intimidate helps Mega Gengar survive moves that would hit it for heavy damage like Earthquake from Garchomp. Fake Out makes it safer to set up Perish Song, and Throat Chop threatens Ghost-types while stopping opposing Incineroar from switching out with Parting Shot. Incineroar can weaken almost any foe with its own Parting Shot, which can be also used after Mega Gengar switches out to bring Mega Gengar back in and preserve the Shadow Tag trap. Maushold has Friend Guard to help with Mega Gengar's mediocre bulk, and it's a fast Encore user to combine with Mega Gengar's Disable, completely shutting down slow foes like Kingambit and Incineroar. Kommo-o's Soundproof makes it immune to Perish Song allowing it to fight alongside Mega Gengar, and it can threaten Dark-types like Kingambit and Incineroar with heavy damage by using Aura Sphere. Mega Gengar can in turn use Disable on the Fairy-types that threaten Kommo-o or threaten them directly with Sludge Bomb. Politoed is useful as a secondary Perish Song setter, and it can rewrite Mega Charizard Y's Drought with Drizzle. Sinistcha's Hospitality and Life Dew are great healing options that help sustain a Perish Song and Kommo-o mode, and it can protect its partners with Rage Powder.

  • How to Overcome Your Weaknesses: Maushold's Follow Me stops Mega Gengar from being Taunted, and it specifically redirects the aforementioned Ghost-type attacks that would OHKO Mega Gengar into an immune target. Fake Out is pivotal for stopping foes like Kingambit for a turn, while Protect and Parting Shot can stall out turns of Perish Song. Protect is important for baiting out foes' attacks like Kowtow Cleave, Volt Switch, and Parting Shot so that they can be Disabled the next turn or locked into a suboptimal move with Encore, so they cannot select a strong attack or pivot move for future turns.

Focus Sash Offensive Support.description:
• Aerodactyl leverages both its high Speed to set Tailwind and STAB Rock Slide to either check metagame staples such as Mega Charizard Y or simply steal turns with flinches. A fast Rock Slide in particular sets Aerodactyl apart from other Tailwind users such as Whimsicott and Talonflame, as Rock-type coverage pairs well with other spread move attackers' STAB moves, such as Garchomp with its Earthquake and Mega Charizard Y with its Heat Wave, making Aerodactyl a key component in these offensive cores.

  • Dual Wingbeat versus Wide Guard: Dual Wingbeat covers Fighting-types that resist Rock Slide, most notably Sneasler, as Aerodactyl is one of the few Pokemon that can outspeed and OHKO it. Dual Wingbeat hitting multiple times cuts through any potential Focus Sash from Sneasler and Whimsicott.

  • Wide Guard protects both Aerodactyl and its partners from opposing Aerodactyl and Garchomp using Rock Slide, which Mega Charizard Y in particular appreciates. It also offers defensive counterplay against other strong spread move users, such as blocking Water Spout Mega Blastoise, Blizzard Mega Froslass and Alolan Ninetales, as well as Hyper Voice Sylveon.

Other Options

  • Taunt: Taunt is a viable option over Dual Wingbeat or even over Protect as a surprise option in a best-of-one setting. Suppressing moves like Trick Room, Follow Me, Rage Powder, and Mega Gengar's Perish Song can stop such strategies without relying on Rock Slide flinches.

Items

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash ensures Aerodactyl can set Tailwind regardless of its common weaknesses. In particular, it ensures that Tailwind is set against faster threats such as Choice Scarf Rotom-Wash, Rotom-Heat, and Basculegion, as well as Sand Rush Excadrill and priority attackers such as Mega Scizor with Bullet Punch.

Abilities

  • Unnerve: Unnerve is uniquely positioned in Regulation M-A, as many commonly used items are berries. Stopping Sitrus Berry from being used helps deal with problematic defensive Pokemon such as Incineroar and Sinistcha, with targets like the latter notably being stopped from activating Sitrus Berry midway through Dual Wingbeat. Unnerve also assists partner attackers such as Mega Charizard Y and Sneasler score in scoring OHKOs despite opposing resist berries such as Occa Berry defensive Whimsicott, Chople Berry Kingambit, and Incineroar's choice of Passho Berry, Chople Berry, or Shuca Berry.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Aerodactyl has many common weaknesses, notably to Water-, Rock-, and Steel-type moves such as Wave Crash, Rock Slide, and Iron Head from Basculegion, Garchomp, and Excadrill. Aerodactyl's Flying typing opens it up to other Rock Slides, especially from Choice Scarf Garchomp and Sand Rush-boosted Excadrill, which outspeed it and resist Aerodactyl's Rock Slide. Excadrill can also use Iron Head to avoid Wide Guard and deal more damage to Aerodactyl. Choice Scarf Basculegion can similarly easily bring it Aerodactyl to Focus Sash before it moves. Non-Choice Scarf Basculegion, while not able to outspeed Aerodactyl, can use Wave Crash or Liquidation to bring it down to Focus Sash, and then attack with Aqua Jet the following turn to finish it off. Priority moves can easily dispatch Aerodactyl after its Focus Sash is broken. Notably, Aerodactyl's typing makes it weak to Bullet Punch from Mega Scizor. Kingambit's unboosted Sucker Punch deals upwards of half Aerodactyl's health, making it similarly effective at finishing off Aerodactyl. Both Kingambit and Aegislash can use Iron Head to easily bring Aerodactyl to Focus Sash before finishing with Sucker Punch and Shadow Sneak, respectively, while resisting Rock Slide and Dual Wingbeat. Wide Guard from Aegislash, Pelipper, and opposing Aerodactyl blocks Rock Slide and is similarly annoying for Aerodactyl's common partners like Heat Wave Mega Charizard Y and Earthquake Garchomp.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Charizard Y weakens Water-type moves and hits Basculegion super effectively with the sun and Solar Beam, respectively. Garchomp covers Steel-types and other common Rock Slide users such as Tyranitar and Excadrill with Earthquake, which it can freely use next to Aerodactyl. Mega Floette and Sylveon are effective Tailwind recipients with their spread Fairy-type attacks and pair well with Dual Wingbeat Aerodactyl, as it can quickly dispatch Sneasler before it can threaten them with Dire Claw.

  • How to Overcome Aerodactyl's Weaknesses: Aerodactyl's checks can actually answer themselves when used in tandem with Aerodactyl. Garchomp and Basculegion can hit opposing Garchomp and Basculegion super effectively with their STAB Dragon Claw or Scale Shot and Last Respects, and hitting first with these moves is easier with Aerodactyl's Tailwind support. Similarly, Kingambit can check opposing Kingambit with Low Kick and threaten an OHKO with Sucker Punch against the ever-present Basculegion. Tailwind generally has a problem with Trick Room, so being able to KO or Taunt Trick Room setters before they can set up is vital. Mega Charizard Y can easily clear Sinistcha and more cleanly KO Farigiraf after Aerodactyl's Rock Slide damage. Kingambit similarly threatens Trick Room users such as the aforementioned two and Mega Gardevoir, hits first regardless of Trick Room with Sucker Punch, and takes advantage of Trick Room itself with its low base Speed. If Trick Room does go up, Wide Guard Aerodactyl can help stall for turns against some common Trick Room attackers such as Primarina, Mega Gardevoir, and Sylveon, all with Hyper Voice, as well as Eruption Torkoal.

Tailwind Setter.description:
• Mega Aerodactyl is the fastest unboosted Pokemon in the metagame, which makes it an incredibly consistent Tailwind setter while also outspeeding and threatening OHKOs on common Pokemon such as Mega Charizard Y and Sneasler.

  • Rock Slide: Mega Aerodactyl is an exceptional user of Rock Slide, since it is able to outspeed and OHKO Mega Charizard Y. Thanks to its incredible Speed, Mega Aerodactyl can consistently threaten flinches with Rock Slide.

  • Dual Wingbeat: Mega Aerodactyl's Dual Wingbeat is incredibly strong thanks to Tough Claws, making it a solid neutral attack against Pokemon like Basculegion-M. Dual Wingbeat is able to OHKO Sneasler, Venusaur, and Whimsicott through their Focus Sash and deal huge damage to Sinistcha and Mega Venusaur.

  • Mega Evolving Aerodactyl: In its base forme, Aerodactyl can still function well as a fast Tailwind setter, so it can be brought to a battle to support another Mega Evolution. Base forme Aerodactyl can also make use of Unnerve to prevent Sitrus Berry on Pokemon like Incineroar and Farigiraf and Chople Berry on Kingambit from activating.

Other Options

  • Ice Fang: Mega Aerodactyl's Ice Fang is able to OHKO Garchomp but isn't very useful against other Pokemon. This move can be run over Tailwind or Protect, which will either remove Mega Aerodactyl's ability to support its teammates or make it more vulnerable to Fake Out.

  • Wide Guard: Wide Guard can be used over Protect to shield partner Mega Charizard Y from opposing Rock Slide and stop other spread moves like Mega Froslass's Blizzard or Garchomp's Earthquake. Dropping Protect makes Mega Aerodactyl more vulnerable, making positioning with it much harder.

Abilities

  • Tough Claws: Tough Claws boosts Mega Aerodactyl's Dual Wingbeat and Ice Fang, allowing the former to OHKO Sneasler and Whimsicott and the latter to OHKO Garchomp.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Mega Aerodactyl is incredibly weak to Steel-types like Kingambit, Archaludon, and Excadrill, which can easily tank any of its attacks and OHKO it back with their Steel-type attacks. Without Ice Fang, Garchomp can be problematic, since it can deal big damage with Rock Slide, and hitting it with Dual Wingbeat will trigger Rough Skin twice. Other Pokemon like Mega Tyranitar and Rotom-Wash can easily tank Mega Aerodactyl's attacks and then threaten big damage back. Choice Scarf Rotom-Wash can be a particularly bad matchup for Mega Aerodactyl, since it can outspeed and threaten heavy damage to Mega Aerodactyl with Thunderbolt or Hydro Pump or slow it down with Electroweb. Mega Aerodactyl is also susceptible to having its damage output reduced by Incineroar's Intimidate and Mega Scovillain's Spicy Spray.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Garchomp is an excellent partner for Mega Aerodactyl, since it can freely use Earthquake next to it and threaten the Steel-types that Mega Aerodactyl struggles against. Sylveon is a great beneficiary of Mega Aerodactyl's Tailwind, with it being able to spam powerful Hyper Voices that threaten Garchomp while Mega Aerodactyl deals with common threats to Sylveon such as Mega Charizard Y and Sneasler. Kingambit is able to deter Pokemon like Incineroar and Farigiraf, which could otherwise slow down Mega Aerodactyl with Intimidate and Trick Room, respectively, while also threatening to deal heavy damage to opposing Kingambit and Mega Tyranitar with Low Kick. Mega Charizard Y works as a great alternative Mega Evolution for Mega Aerodactyl, since it melts through Steel-types and works well with Aerodactyl's base forme. Mega Charizard Y can also handle Mega Evolutions that Mega Aerodactyl might struggle against, such as Mega Scovillain and Mega Floette, while Mega Aerodactyl can deal with Mega Dragonite in return. Farigiraf can block Fake Out thanks to Armor Tail, which is very useful for Mega Aerodactyl sets that aren't running Protect. Farigiraf also blocks Kingambit's Sucker Punch and Basculegion-M's Aqua Jet while being able to reverse Trick Room.

  • How to Overcome Mega Aerodactyl's Weaknesses: Pair Mega Aerodactyl with powerful sweepers to make full use of its fast Tailwind. Pokemon like Garchomp and Sylveon can threaten powerful spread damage on the field while also threatening some of Mega Aerodactyl's checks, such as Archaludon and Mega Tyranitar. Use Mega Aerodactyl to threaten Pokemon like Mega Charizard Y, Sneasler, and Sinistcha, which could otherwise disrupt your offense. Use an alternative Mega Evolution like Mega Charizard Y and Pokemon like Garchomp and Kingambit to deal with matchups where Mega Aerodactyl shouldn't be brought, such as against rain, sand, and Trick Room teams.

Rain Support.description:
• For rain teams, Politoed is a bulky support Pokemon that enables Archaludon while also threatening with Perish Song late-game. Politoed's Drizzle allows it to do well against Fire-types such as Mega Charizard Y, Incineroar, and Mega Delphox by weakening their attacks and allowing Politoed to pressure them with Weather Ball. Meanwhile, Perish Song pressures foes late-game, as they have limited opportunities to switch.

  • Weather Ball: Weather Ball gives Politoed a reliable single-target attack in rain, letting it pressure Fire-types such as Incineroar, Mega Charizard Y, and Mega Delphox without relying entirely on its partner for damage. On teams with Mega Froslass, Weather Ball allows Politoed to pressure Garchomp if rain has been replaced with snow.

  • Perish Song: Perish Song forces opponents to reposition their Pokemon or risk losing both of them. Mega Gengar can trap targets so that they cannot escape Perish Song normally. Protect helps Politoed stall turns and avoid being removed before the Perishing count finishes.

  • Hypnosis versus Ice Beam versus Encore: Hypnosis can temporarily remove a key threat from play and give Politoed's partner room to attack or set up, though its poor accuracy makes it unreliable. Ice Beam gives Politoed consistent coverage against Garchomp, Dragonite, and Sinistcha regardless of the active weather. Encore punishes passive moves like Protect, Trick Room, and setup moves, which is especially useful when the opponent attempts to stall out rain.

Other Options

  • Muddy Water: Muddy Water can be used over Weather Ball for spread damage and accuracy drops, which can be useful when Politoed wants to support its partner while still attacking. However, Muddy Water's lower power makes Politoed worse at immediately pressuring Fire-types like Incineroar and Mega Charizard Y.

  • Helping Hand: Helping Hand compensates for Politoed's limited offensive presence by boosting a partner's attack. It notably amplifies Archaludon's wallbreaking power, allowing +1 Flash Cannon to OHKO bulky Mega Floette and Sylveon and Electro Shot to OHKO bulky Rotom-Wash.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry, in combination with the given defensive spread, gives Politoed the longevity to use Perish Song and stall its turns with Protect while remaining healthy enough to switch out and reset rain later. It notably prevents Adamant Black Glasses Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave and Timid Mega Floette's Moonblast from 2HKOing Politoed.

  • Mystic Water: Mystic Water should be used with an offensive spread, as it further strengthens Politoed's rain-boosted Weather Ball. This gives Politoed much greater immediate offensive pressure at the cost of Sitrus Berry's longevity.

SP Spreads

  • 31 HP / 23 Def / 12 SpD with Calm: 31 HP SPs let Sitrus Berry activate immediately after Politoed gets hit by Maushold's Super Fang. 12 Special Defense SPs let Politoed survive Modest Mega Floette's Light of Ruin from full health. The remaining SPs are invested in Defense, giving Politoed a solid chance to survive Adamant Basculegion-M's 150-Base Power Last Respects while improving its ability to take physical attacks from Garchomp and Sneasler.

  • 32 HP / 2 Def / 32 SpA with Modest: This spread maximizes Politoed's Special Attack while maintaining bulk. It should be used with Mystic Water to strengthen Politoed's rain-boosted Weather Ball enough to guarantee OHKOs on offensive Sneasler and specially bulky Incineroar. The Special Attack investment also allows Ice Beam to always OHKO offensive Garchomp.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Politoed struggles against strong Electric- and Grass-type attacks from Pokemon such as Archaludon and Sinistcha, both of which take little damage from Weather Ball. Opposing weather setters like Mega Charizard Y, Mega Tyranitar, Mega Froslass, and Torkoal can also remove rain, stopping your own Archaludon from using Electro Shot. Without Ice Beam, Politoed also struggles to threaten Dragon-types such as Hydreigon and Mega Dragonite, which can deal heavy damage to it with Draco Meteor and Dragon Pulse, respectively.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Archaludon is the main rain sweeper, using Politoed's rain to fire off Electro Shot immediately and threaten Water- and Flying-types such as Basculegion-M, Milotic, and Aerodactyl. Espathra is a great partner on Baton Pass rain teams, passing Speed and Calm Mind boosts to Archaludon so that it can snowball much more easily once Politoed sets rain. Mega Gengar is the main partner on Perish Song archetypes; it traps foes so that they cannot freely switch out. Incineroar and Sneasler provide Fake Out support to help Politoed use Perish Song or land Hypnosis. Sinistcha gives Politoed teams redirection and Hospitality recovery, while Mega Froslass can set Aurora Veil and reset rain later with Rain Dance.

  • How to Overcome Politoed's Weaknesses: Politoed should be preserved carefully in weather wars against Mega Charizard Y, Mega Tyranitar, and Mega Froslass, as maintaining weather control makes these foes far easier for Politoed to deal with. Mega Dragonite can handle Mega Charizard Y, Sneasler threatens Mega Tyranitar with Close Combat, and Kingambit deals with Mega Froslass. Additionally, your own Mega Froslass can use Rain Dance to restore rain without forcing Politoed back onto the field. Against Electric- and Grass-types, Politoed should avoid sitting on the field and instead use Protect, Encore, or Hypnosis, or it should switch out to better position itself later on. Archaludon resists both Electric- and Grass-type attacks and can switch into moves such as Electro Shot from opposing Archaludon and Matcha Gotcha from Sinistcha, accumulating Stamina boots to make itself progressively more difficult to remove with physical attacks, while Incineroar resists Grass-type attacks and threatens Sinistcha. Perish Song should usually be saved for late-game scenarios or situations where the opponent has limited switching options, such as times when Mega Gengar is trapping a target. Sneasler’s Fake Out and Politoed’s Protect can also safely stall turns of the Perishing count.

Sand Attacker.description:
• Mega Tyranitar bolsters a team against opposing weather strategies while boasting good matchups against common Fire-types like Mega Delphox and Incineroar as well as Trick Room staples like Farigiraf and Torkoal.

  • Low Kick versus Dragon Dance: Low Kick threatens Kingambit and opposing Mega Tyranitar. Low Kick Mega Tyranitar is a good Kingambit check, as it outspeeds Kingambit, resists Sucker Punch, and has great physical bulk. Dropping Low Kick for Dragon Dance turns Mega Tyranitar into a game-ending threat when given support in the form of redirection from Sinistcha and damage mitigation from Rotom-Wash and Incineroar. Dragon Dance also enables Mega Tyranitar to go for Rock Slide flinches against a greater number of Pokemon. However, the rest of the team must have a better matchup against Kingambit without Tyranitar's Low Kick.

  • Mega Evolving Tyranitar: Tyranitar should look to Mega Evolve when it knows that it can win the weather war. If it leads against a Froslass holding Froslassite or Charizard holding Charizardite Y, then it should try to Mega Evolve either on the same turn as them or a turn after them. This ensures that sand will be up and these Pokemon cannot benefit from the weather they set. The state of the weather when leading against Pelipper is a bit tricky; fast Tyranitar sets will always concede the early weather advantage, and slow, bulky Pelipper sets will always seize weather control. Tyranitar can Mega Evolve to re-establish weather should rain win out after the lead.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 13 Atk / 4 Def / 17 Spe with Adamant: 17 Speed SPs allow Mega Tyranitar to outspeed Choice Scarf Basculegion-M under Tailwind. The physical bulk ensures that Mega Tyranitar always survives Jolly Adaptability Basculegion-M's Wave Crash. This bulky spread is best used with Low Kick.

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Jolly: Maximizing Speed and power lets Mega Tyranitar make the most of the boosts granted by Dragon Dance.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Fighting-types like Sneasler and Fairy-types like Mega Floette and Sylveon directly threaten Mega Tyranitar; it struggles to effectively hit these Pokemon, especially Sneasler. Mega Tyranitar is also not particularly fast, so many attackers get the chance to attack it before it can respond. This includes threats like Garchomp, which is also unthreatened by Mega Tyranitar's attacks, even surviving Knock Off from Mega Tyranitar at +1 Attack. While Mega Tyranitar is excellent at disrupting rain, Pokemon on rain teams like Archaludon and Basculegion-M threaten it with their STAB attacks. Finally, Chople Berry variants of Kingambit can turn the tables on Mega Tyranitar by surviving Low Kick and OHKOing it in return with Iron Head.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Tyranitar benefits from having Ghost- and Steel-types that can check the Fighting- and Fairy-types it is afraid of. One of its best partners is Sinistcha, which can redirect away Fighting- and Water-type attacks and set Trick Room to let Mega Tyranitar outspeed Pokemon it otherwise could not, such as Archaludon. Corviknight is strong against Fairy- and Fighting-types, packs Speed control in the form of Tailwind, and resists Garchomp's STAB moves. Pokemon like Rotom-Wash, Hydreigon, and the aforementioned Sinistcha that threaten common Pokemon on rain teams ensure that Mega Tyranitar does not entirely rely on winning the weather war. Similarly, Pokemon that can back up Mega Tyranitar in the fight against Mega Charizard Y's sun, like Garchomp, Hydreigon, and Incineroar, ensure that it isn't alone in attempting to hold off dangerous sun threats. Mega Tyranitar's sand also enables Sand Rush Excadrill, a fast cleaner that beats Mega Tyranitar checks like Sneasler and Mega Floette.

  • How to Overcome Mega Tyranitar's Weaknesses: Mega Tyranitar has a middling Speed tier, meaning that it is slower than many Pokemon. Speed control in the form of Sinistcha's Trick Room or Corviknight's Tailwind lets Mega Tyranitar threaten a greater number of Pokemon. Sinistcha's redirection also allows Mega Tyranitar to bypass otherwise super effective attacks. Steel-types like Corviknight and Excadrill threaten Fairy-types like Mega Floette and Sylveon that threaten Mega Tyranitar.

Glass Cannon.description:
• Mega Blaziken's high Speed and Attack give it a good matchup against metagame staples like Incineroar, Kingambit, and Gholdengo. With Speed Boost, it can essentially guarantee it is the fastest Pokemon on the field after enough turns have passed, outspeeding Mega Aerodactyl and slower Pokemon like Sylveon even if they have a boost from Tailwind.

  • Rock Slide: Rock Slide OHKOes Mega Charizard Y. Combined with Speed Boost, Rock Slide lets Mega Blaziken threaten flinches before foes can move.

  • Detect: Detect is mandatory to safely gain Speed boosts.

Other Options

  • Swords Dance: Swords Dance can be used to offset Intimidate from Incineroar and make Mega Blaziken strong enough to OHKO Garchomp with Close Combat at +1 Attack. It can replace Rock Slide on teams that have another way to cover Mega Charizard Y, such as Mega Aerodactyl.

SP Spreads

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant: Speed Boost allows Adamant Mega Blaziken to outspeed Mega Aerodactyl after one turn.

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Jolly: Opting for a Jolly nature allows Mega Blaziken to always outspeed Sylveon under Tailwind after one turn.

Teambuilding

  • Rain Matchup: Mega Swampert threatens to OHKO Mega Blaziken with either STAB attack, and Swift Swim lets it outspeed Mega Blaziken in the rain even after a turn of Speed Boost. Basculegion-M and Pelipper resist both of Mega Blaziken's STAB attacks and respond with an OHKO from Wave Crash and Hurricane or Weather Ball, respectively; Pelipper also weakens Flare Blitz while enabling Mega Swampert with Drizzle.

  • Other Weaknesses: Garchomp threatens an OHKO with Earthquake, which cannot be redirected by Sinistcha's Rage Powder. Mega Aerodactyl threatens an OHKO with Dual Wingbeat and can use Tailwind before Mega Blaziken gets its Speed Boost to deny Mega Blaziken's Speed advantage. Whimsicott has Tailwind to negate Mega Blaziken's Speed advantage and Encore to punish it for using Detect to gain Speed Boosts. Opposing Trick Room uses Mega Blaziken's Speed Boost against it, and Farigiraf threatens to OHKO it with Psychic. Mega Staraptor enters the field with Intimidate, threatens an OHKO with Brave Bird, and is often paired with Whimsicott to negate Mega Blaziken's Speed Boost with Tailwind. Mega Delphox threatens an OHKO with Psychic or Psyshock. Ceruledge completely walls both of Mega Blaziken's STAB attacks.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Basculegion-M has a better matchup against rain teams and Mega Aerodactyl, while Mega Blaziken helps it against Archaludon. Weather setters like Alolan Ninetales and Torkoal overwrite rain; Alolan Ninetales handles Garchomp with Blizzard; and Torkoal is useful in Trick Room while providing sun to let Flare Blitz OHKO bulky variants of Sylveon and offensive variants of Farigiraf. Sinistcha can nearly OHKO Mega Swampert with Matcha Gotcha and use Rage Powder to redirect threatening attacks like Pelipper's Weather Ball and Basculegion-M's Wave Crash. It can also redirect neutral attacks that threaten Mega Blaziken due to its low bulk, like Sneasler's Dire Claw and Close Combat. Sinistcha helps offset Flare Blitz recoil with Hospitality and can also reverse Trick Room. Mega Blaziken, in turn, handles Kingambit, which threatens Sinistcha.

  • Kingambit threatens to OHKO Basculegion-M with Sucker Punch and is comfortable against Mega Aerodactyl, Mega Delphox, and Ceruledge, as it can survive their attacks and either OHKO them in return or deal enough damage to finish them off with Sucker Punch. Due to Defiant, Kingambit's presence can also deter Incineroar from switching in and activating Intimidate against Mega Blaziken. In return, Mega Blaziken handles Mega Charizard Y for Kingambit with Rock Slide. Sylveon is a strong answer to Garchomp, and Mega Blaziken, in turn, handles Steel-types that threaten Sylveon, such as Gholdengo and Mega Metagross.

  • Alternative Mega Evolutions: Mega Aerodactyl can take the place of Mega Blaziken against teams with nuisances like Garchomp, Mega Delphox, Ceruledge, and opposing Mega Aerodactyl. Mega Blaziken complements Mega Aerodactyl by beating its counters: Mega Tyranitar, Mega Metagross, and Mega Mawile. Mega Froslass has a better matchup against rain teams by setting snow over rain, and it is also strong against Garchomp and the combination of Mega Staraptor and Whimsicott. Mega Blaziken also plays well against Mega Froslass's counters: Mega Charizard Y, Kingambit, and Incineroar.

Fast Offense.description:
• Mega Swampert gives rain teams a clear choice of Mega Evolution, using its newly granted access to Wave Crash to hit incredibly hard. It is able to OHKO most Pokemon in Regulation M-B that do not resist Wave Crash in rain, albeit at the cost of a large portion of its own HP. It boasts a strong matchup against Regulation M-B staples such as Incineroar, Mega Metagross, and Sneasler.

  • Swift Swim: Swift Swim allows Mega Swampert to outrun every unboosted Pokemon in the tier when rain is active. This means it outspeeds the likes of Garchomp and Mega Raichu Y, two Pokemon that would otherwise greatly burden its partners. Mega Swampert can OHKO them before Garchomp threatens partner Archaludon with Earthquake or Mega Raichu Y threatens Archaludon and Pelipper with Focus Blast and Zap Cannon, respectively.

  • Ice Punch: Ice Punch allows Mega Swampert to threaten the Grass-types that OHKO it, such as Sinistcha, as well as Garchomp, which would otherwise deal a large amount of damage to Mega Swampert through the combination of Wave Crash recoil and Rough Skin contact damage. Notably, it is able to OHKO Whimsicott after Fake Out breaks its Focus Sash, preventing it from setting Tailwind and allowing Mega Swampert to maintain its Speed advantage in rain. It also allows Mega Swampert to hit the occasional Mega Dragonite for heavy damage.

  • Ground-type moves: While some Mega Swampert opt to run only Earthquake, others run High Horsepower to hit Steel-types such as Kingambit without threatening their partner. High Horsepower can be run instead of Earthquake, replacing it as the only Ground-type move, or instead of Ice Punch, forgoing coverage.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Mega Swampert heavily relies on rain to boost its damage output and Speed. Without it, Mega Swampert can struggle to survive specific attacks such as Solar Beam from Mega Charizard Y or secure certain OHKOs. As such, one of its most problematic foes is Mega Charizard Y. If Mega Charizard Y catches Mega Swampert in sun, it can outspeed and OHKO it with Solar Beam, while Mega Swampert cannot OHKO bulky Mega Charizard Y in sun even after surviving Solar Beam.

  • Grass-type threats: Sinistcha can also be a problem, as Mega Swampert struggles to even 2HKO physically bulky Sinistcha with Ice Punch, while Sinistcha can threaten massive damage to Mega Swampert with Matcha Gotcha and is immune to Fake Out and Rage Powder. Venusaur is also able to survive Ice Punch and retaliate with Giga Drain or another Grass-type move.

  • Basculegion-M: Basculegion-M can take advantage of Mega Swampert's preferred weather and threaten an OHKO with rain-boosted Wave Crash while avoiding an OHKO from High Horsepower or Earthquake.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Swampert synergizes well with Archaludon, as Mega Swampert is able to outspeed and OHKO Archaludon's biggest counters in Garchomp, Mega Raichu Y, and Sneasler, while Archaludon resists the Grass-type moves that threaten Mega Swampert. Archaludon can also take Wave Crash from Basculegion-M and retaliate with Electro Shot in rain while bolstering its Defense with Stamina. However, both Pokemon heavily rely on the weather being in their favor to successfully win these matchups.

  • Drizzle Pokemon: Mega Swampert is run exclusively on teams featuring either Pelipper or Politoed, as it is simply not worth using unless it is on a rain-focused team. It is usually run with Pelipper, as Pelipper can threaten the Grass-types that threaten Mega Swampert with Hurricane while being immune to Mega Swampert's Earthquake.

  • Dual screens setters: Mega Swampert is often paired with Grimmsnarl or Sableye, as their Light Screen and Reflect help Archaludon and Mega Swampert stay on the field. Using Rain Dance with Sableye guarantees that rain will be active that turn, as Sableye moves after Mega Charizard YMega Evolves or switches in and sets sun.

  • Redirection: Sinistcha helps Mega Swampert's common partner Archaludon with its Ground-type resistance and ability to set Trick Room, allowing Archaludon to move before threats such as Garchomp. On top of that, Sinistcha can quickly dispatch opposing Mega Swampert, a matchup that can be volatile for Mega Swampert and partner Archaludon. It is also able to redirect and resist Wave Crash from Basculegion-M.

Bulky Support.description:
• Pelipper is the premier rain setter of Regulation M-A. Being on the slower side, it is able to lead against opposing weather setters like Alolan Ninetales and have the rain override whatever the opposing weather is. Thanks to its Flying typing, it can threaten Grass-types like Sinistcha that otherwise spell trouble for rain teams.

  • Weather Ball: Weather Ball threatens foes like Incineroar in rain, though it is useful in other weathers as well. For example, if the snow is set up, Weather Ball is capable of OHKOing opposing Garchomp.

  • Hurricane: Hurricane is fully accurate in the rain, putting pressure on Grass-types like Sinistcha. Pelipper must be wary of using Hurricane, however, as it becomes rather unreliable if an opposing weather setter overrides the rain with their weather. It is also possible to use Hurricane to fish for confusion for a win, though this isn't to be relied on unless it is the only way out.

  • Protect versus Wide Guard: Protect allows Pelipper to better position itself, setting up the rain more easily. Wide Guard, on the other hand, protects Pelipper and its partners from powerful spread moves such as Rock Slide from Mega Aerodactyl and Dazzling Gleam from Mega Floette.

  • Weather Wars: Because of the abundance of weather within Regulation M-A, you must be careful when using Pelipper. Keeping it in the back to obtain weather control late-game will make it far easier to win, while leading off with your weather and forcing the opposing weather setter to swap in can leave them vulnerable.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry allows Pelipper to nearly always avoid being 2HKOed by Dazzling Gleam from Timid Mega Floette and Wave Crash from Adamant Adaptability Basculegion-M in the rain.

Abilities

  • Drizzle: Drizzle enables partners like Archaludon and Basculegion-M while also shutting down opposing weather from the likes of Mega Charizard Y and Mega Tyranitar.

SP Spreads

  • 31 HP / 14 Def / 18 SpD / 3 Spe with Calm: The given SP spread ensures Pelipper survives Moonblast from Mega Floette or 150-Base Power Last Respects from Jolly Basculegion-M while giving it a good chance to survive Power Gem from Timid Glimmora. The Speed SPs allow Pelipper to outrun uninvested Corviknight.

  • 31 HP / 14 Def / 2 SpA / 16 SpD / 3 Spe with Modest: The Speed and Defense benchmarks are the same as the previous spread, but with Modest, Pelipper will always OHKO Mega Delphox and low-bulk Sneasler with Rain-boosted Weather Ball and Hurricane, respectively. The Special Defense and HP SPs allow Pelipper to survive Moonblast from Timid Mega Floette.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Dragon-types like Mega Dragonite and Archaludon can easily tank a Weather Ball and retaliate with Draco Meteor, threatening Pelipper on its lower Special Defense. Opposing weather also can be a struggle, forcing Pelipper to swap out and possibly leaving it open to be predicted and KOed when attempting to swap back in. Mega Pokemon that set weather, notably Mega Tyranitar, Mega Froslass, and Mega Charizard Y, handily override Pelipper's rain mid-turn via Mega Evolution. Rotom-Wash resists both of Pelipper's STAB moves and can OHKO it with Thunderbolt, while Milotic can tank attacks and put it to sleep with Hypnosis, leaving it open to be KOed.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Archaludon is very helpful against Dragon- and Water-types that annoy Pelipper, hitting them hard with Draco Meteor and Electro Shot, respectively. Additionally, it threatens Mega Tyranitar, Mega Froslass, and Alolan Ninetales with Flash Cannon, all of which are opposing weather setters. Basculegion-M can also threaten opposing weather setters, even having the capability of OHKOing Mega Charizard Y in the sun with Wave Crash. In return, Pelipper can set up the rain for both of these, allowing Archaludon's Electro Shot and Basculegion's Wave Crash to become far more threatening.

  • Mega Venusaur threatens Pokemon like Mega Floette that may hit Pelipper for big damage and the Water-types that disrupt it. Thanks to Pelipper, Mega Venusaur can sit in the rain to avoid being majorly threatened by Fire-type attacks from the likes of Mega Charizard Y and Incineroar. Mega Lopunny can more freely fire off attacks due to Pelipper's ability to threaten Pokemon like Sneasler and Mega Scovillain, all while providing Fake Out support to protect Pelipper when switching in. Incineroar also provides Fake Out support as well as a slower pivot option with Parting Shot, getting Pelipper in safely.

  • How to Overcome Pelipper's Weaknesses: Attempting to remove opposing weather should be a top priority to allow Pelipper to shine. Partners like the occasional Mega Scovillain, Sinistcha, and Incineroar provide redirection, slow pivoting, and Fake Out support, all of which allow Pelipper to swap in safely. Pelipper should most often be brought in the back against opposing weather teams to try and ensure that rain will be the dominant weather. Against non-weather teams, leading Pelipper with a strong rain Pokemon like Basculegion-M can apply lots of pressure early-game.

Bulky Attacker.description:
• Mega Gardevoir uses Pixilate-boosted Hyper Voice in tandem with its high Special Attack to become a potent spread attacker, threatening the likes of Garchomp, Dragonite, and Hydreigon with heavy damage. Its Psychic-type STAB options notably OHKO Sneasler and threaten Toxapex, while Trick Room allows it to support itself and its team, differentiating it from Mega Floette and Sylveon, which provide competition for the Fairy-type slot.

  • Psyshock versus Psychic: Psyshock allows Mega Gardevoir to hit certain foes on their weaker Defense, notably 2HKOing Sylveon, Mega Floette, and bulky Mega Charizard Y, whereas Psychic secures important 2HKOs on Sinistcha, Mega Scovillain, and Mega Froslass.

  • Trick Room versus Calm Mind: Trick Room allows Mega Gardevoir to support its slower partners, most notably Kingambit, and also benefits Mega Gardevoir against fast offensive teams. Calm Mind allows Mega Gardevoir to become a potent sweeper while shoring up its special bulk. After a single boost, Mega Gardevoir can 2HKO Incineroar with Hyper Voice and OHKO no-bulk Basculegion-M with either Psychic or Psyshock.

Other Options

  • Vacuum Wave: Vacuum Wave gives Mega Gardevoir a priority option that threatens Kingambit with heavy damage while moving before Sucker Punch and invalidating it, as well as picking off weakened foes, notably Aerodactyl and Lycanroc-D brought down to Focus Sash.

Abilities

  • Trace versus Telepathy: Trace gives Mega Gardevoir the potential to copy very useful abilities, such as Intimidate from Incineroar, Chlorophyll from Venusaur, and Armor Tail from Farigiraf. This can also incentivize Mega Gardevoir not to Mega Evolve immediately. Telepathy allows Mega Gardevoir to avoid Earthquake from partner Garchomp.

SP Spreads

  • 16 HP / 2 Def / 32 SpA / 16 Spe with Modest: This spread allows Mega Gardevoir to survive Sucker Punch from +1 Kingambit, Kowtow Cleave from Black Glasses Kingambit most of the time, Weather Ball from Mega Charizard Y in sun, or Light of Ruin from Timid Mega Floette. The Speed investment allows Mega Gardevoir to outspeed Adamant Dragonite and Adamant Basculegion-M.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Sneasler, Mega Gengar, and Choice Scarf Basculegion-M can outspeed and OHKO Mega Gardevoir with Dire Claw, Sludge Bomb, and Last Respects, respectively. Focus Sash or Sitrus Berry variants of Basculegion-M can take any attack from Mega Gardevoir and OHKO it in return with Last Respects.
