Mega Charizard Y and Mega Delphox can comfortably take Hyper Voice and heavily damage Mega Gardevoir in return with powerful Fire-type STAB moves, with the latter also resisting Psychic-type attacks. Kingambit, too, can take Hyper Voice and threaten an OHKO with Iron Head. Wide Guard from foes such as Aerodactyl and Aegislash can be very problematic for Mega Gardevoir, shutting down its main damage source in Hyper Voice ; Aegislash can also severely threaten Mega Gardevoir with its Steel- and Ghost-type STAB moves.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Garchomp is a premier partner for Mega Gardevoir, as its Ground-type STAB moves threaten Sneasler, Mega Gengar, and Kingambit, all of which are problematic for Mega Gardevoir. In return, Mega Gardevoir threatens opposing Dragon-types like Dragonite and Hydreigon that threaten Garchomp. Maushold is another amazing partner, as it supports Mega Gardevoir with Follow Me and is notably immune to Ghost-type attacks that threaten Mega Gardevoir, such as Poltergeist from Aegislash and Last Respects from Basculegion-M; it can also damage foes with Super Fang to put them in range of Hyper Voice. Basculegion-M enjoys Mega Gardevoir's ability to threaten Dark-types with Pixilate-boosted Hyper Voice and can threaten Mega Charizard Y and Sneasler in return, though the two share a check in Kingambit. Mega Gardevoir loves Tailwind from partners like Talonflame and Aerodactyl to allow it to outspeed and OHKO faster foes, most importantly Sneasler and Garchomp. Mega Gardevoir also enjoys Fake Out support from partners such as Sneasler and Incineroar to keep it safe and potentially allow it to use Trick Room or set up with Calm Mind.

  • How to Overcome Mega Gardevoir's Weaknesses: Mega Gardevoir's physical susceptibility can be alleviated by Intimidate from partner Incineroar or redirection from Maushold and Sinistcha. Speed control like Tailwind from Talonflame or Trick Room from either Mega Gardevoir itself or Sinistcha can allow it to outspeed and heavily damage offensive checks such as Choice Scarf Basculegion-M and Mega Gengar. Partners that threaten Fairy-resistant foes, including Ground-types like Garchomp and Fire-types like Incineroar, are crucial in applying pressure throughout the game and allowing Mega Gardevoir to use Hyper Voice more safely.

Screens Support.description:
• Sableye aims to support its allies while disrupting foes, using dual screens to allow its allies to survive attacks they couldn't otherwise and boasting a great type matchup against Sneasler.

  • Rain Dance: Rain Dance is used to shut down weather set by the likes of Mega Charizard Y, Mega Froslass, and Mega Tyranitar, allowing allies like Archaludon and Basculegion-M to thrive. It also allows for mix-ups, removing the need to bring Pelipper or Politoed to every game to set rain.

  • Encore versus Foul Play: Encore provides more disruptive tools for Sableye, punishing foes for playing passively with Protect or locking foes into setup moves. Foul Play, on the other hand, grants Sableye a damaging option so it doesn't get fully shut down by Taunt; Foul Play can OHKO Adamant Basculegion-M.

Other Options

  • Disable: Disable is usable on sets that forgo dual screens and opt to run Sableye as disruptive support, forcing foes to use Struggle when paired with Encore. This does, however, come at the cost of Sableye becoming more of a sitting duck, as it now cannot help its allies defensively.

  • Fake Out: Fake Out is great on Sableye, as, thanks to its Ghost typing, it doesn't have to compete in Speed wars with other Fake Out users. However, this comes at the cost of either Reflect, Light Screen, or the last slot and forces Sableye to switch in and out for Fake Out to be useful.

  • Quash: Quash grants Sableye speed control, allowing slower allies like Archaludon to OHKO faster foes like Garchomp with Draco Meteor. It is typically used over the last slot to allow Sableye and Archaludon to become a devastating combination.

  • Will-O-Wisp: Will-O-Wisp allows Sableye to cripple physical attackers, notably Pokemon like Sneasler and Garchomp. However, it does not work on key threats like Kingambit, Mega Tyranitar, or Ceruledge.

Items

  • Roseli Berry: Roseli Berry allows Sableye to survive Fairy-type attacks that would otherwise threaten to OHKO it, including Hyper Voice from Sylveon as well as Moonblast and Dazzling Gleam from Mega Floette.

Abilities

  • Prankster: Prankster allows Sableye to use Reflect or Light Screen before opposing Pokemon move and to change the weather with Rain Dance before opposing weather Pokemon, such as Mega Charizard Y, can attack. Because Rain Dance is used after opposing Pokemon Mega Evolve, unlike Drizzle from Pelipper and Politoed, Sableye can easily flip weather against Mega Tyranitar, Mega Froslass, and Mega Charizard Y.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 17 Def / 17 SpD with Careful: The given SP spread allows Sableye to survive Moonblast from Timid Mega Floette with Roseli Berry and almost always survive Wave Crash from Jolly non-Mystic Water Basculegion-M. Additionally, it survives attacks such as Kowtow Cleave from +1 non-Black Glasses Kingambit and Bitter Blade from +1 Ceruledge.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Sableye is easily countered by many Dark-types in the format, namely Pokemon like Mega Tyranitar, Kingambit, and Incineroar, as they are immune to Sableye's Prankster moves, resist Foul Play, and can retaliate with Knock Off, Kowtow Cleave, or Flare Blitz, respectively. Strong enough Fairy-type attacks, like a boosted Moonblast from Mega Floette, Light of Ruin from Mega Floette, or Hyper Beam from Sylveon, still threaten to OHKO Sableye despite Roseli Berry. Additionally, Sableye tends to struggle to provide enough offensive pressure, as it is totally reliant on its partners to deal all of the damage.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Venusaur greatly appreciates Sableye's capability to bolster its bulk further with dual screens and shut off sun to prevent Mega Charizard Y from becoming too threatening. In return, Mega Venusaur threatens the many Fairy-types that Sableye fears. Archaludon similarly appreciates the dual screens and rain provided by Sableye and can threaten Fairy-types while also breaking through Mega Tyranitar and Incineroar; boosted Electro Shot can help blast through Kingambit. Basculegion-M also loves rain while dealing formidable damage that can mitigate Sableye's passivity. Additionally, Reflect from Sableye allows Basculegion-M to survive Sucker Punch from Kingambit.

  • How to Overcome Sableye's Weaknesses: Sableye prefers to be next to a Pokemon that dishes out large amounts of damage at all times; otherwise, the board state will be too passive and will likely leave its team on the back foot. Archaludon, Basculegion-M, and Mega Scizor all excel at this role. Sableye also needs help handling Fairy-type Pokemon, so partners like the aforementioned Mega Venusaur serve it well.

Fast Sweeper.description:
• Mega Metagross boasts good stats and a very beneficial ability in Tough Claws, which allow it to spearhead entire matchups with its raw single-target damage while taking out its checks with its various coverage moves. Mega Metagross's useful Steel typing lets it take on the format's Fairy-type Pokemon such as Sylveon and Mega Floette with ease.

  • Iron Head vs. Bullet Punch: On teams without prominent speed control, Bullet Punch is an alternative to Iron Head that allows Mega Metagross to secure a KO on faster Pokemon at low health, such as Aerodactyl, Whimsicott, and Sneasler after activating Focus Sash.

  • Body Press vs. Ice Punch vs. Stomping Tantrum: These moves allow Mega Metagross to beat Kingambit and Incineroar, Garchomp, and Ceruledge, respectively. Choosing a coverage move largely depends on how well Mega Metagross's partners perform against these Pokemon. For example, if Mega Metagross is partnered with a Garchomp, opting for Ice Punch can help Garchomp consistently win a mirror matchup without relying on a Speed tie, while Garchomp already covers Kingambit with Earthquake.

  • Mega Evolving Metagross: With Clear Body, Metagross is able to shrug off Intimidate from Incineroar. As such, if the opponent has an Incineroar, it is wise to delay Metagross's Mega Evolution until Metagross actually attacks or Incineroar has already switched in, as this prevents Incineroar from easily lowering Mega Metagross's Attack stat.

SP Spreads

  • 27 Atk / 14 Def / 25 Spe with Jolly: Generally, this SP spread is only worth running if Mega Metagross is also using Body Press. The Defense investment allows it to always OHKO Kingambit with Body Press, while the Speed investment allows it to always outspeed Garchomp and Mega Floette.

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Jolly: This SP spread is used when Mega Metagross is running either Stomping Tantrum or Ice Punch, as Body Press cannot consistently OHKO Kingambit without any Defense investment and is thus not worth running. The extra Attack investment allows it to almost always 2HKO uninvested Basculegion-M with Psychic Fangs, even at -1. The Speed investment allows Mega Metagross to outspeed Alolan Ninetales, letting Metagross OHKO it with Iron Head.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Mega Metagross relies on outspeeding and OHKOing its checks. Basculegion-M poses a problem for this gameplan, as Mega Metagross cannot OHKO it with Psychic Fangs, while Choice Scarf Basculegion-M can outspeed Mega Metagross and threaten an OHKO with 100-Base Power Last Respects. Mega Metagross can beat non-Choice Scarf Basculegion-M only if a partner chips it beforehand.

  • Other Mega Evolutions: Mega Delphox resists both of Mega Metagross's STAB moves while outspeeding Mega Metagross and threatening heavy damage with Heat Wave. Bulky Mega Gengar can threaten a KO on Mega Metagross with Shadow Ball after some chip damage while outspeeding it. Mega Swampert can take any attack from Mega Metagross and has a slight chance to OHKO it with High Horsepower or Earthquake, as well as outspeeding it if the rain is up. Mega Charizard Y is also able to survive Psychic Fangs and can retaliate with sun-boosted Heat Wave or Weather Ball, OHKOing Mega Metagross.

  • Coverage Move Trade-offs: As Mega Metagross cannot fit all of its coverage moves onto its set, it is important to be aware of Metagross's negative matchups depending on the selected coverage option and take these into account when building around Metagross.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Metagross is often used on rain teams, as Drizzle or Rain Dance can make Mega Charizard Y reposition or allow Mega Metagross to survive a Heat Wave or Weather Ball. Common rain staples such as Mega Swampert also boast an excellent matchup against Mega Gengar, Mega Delphox, and Mega Charizard Y. Additionally, Ice Punch Mega Metagross can cover Garchomp, which would otherwise threaten Archaludon, a rain staple.

  • Mega Metagross as a Matchup Fixer: On other teams, such as those with Mega Charizard Y, Mega Metagross can be used as a secondary Mega Evolution option to handle foes such as Toxapex and opposing weather setters like Mega Tyranitar and Mega Froslass.

Contrary Sweeper.description:
• Mega Staraptor uses its high Attack, solid Speed tier, and offensive typing to threaten metagame staples such as Kingambit, Incineroar, and Sneasler. With Contrary and Close Combat, it can make itself difficult to remove after multiple boosts to its defenses. It can even support its team with Tailwind and Intimidate prior to Mega Evolving.

  • Contrary and Close Combat: Contrary punishes Incineroar's Intimidate, and combining Contrary with Close Combat allows Mega Staraptor to threaten Incineroar even more while boosting its defenses.

  • Roost versus Tailwind: Roost makes Mega Staraptor even more difficult to remove after a boost to its defenses and helps it take attacks like Electro Shot from Archaludon more effectively. Roost can be used on any team, even if it lacks speed control, and Tailwind is less necessary on teams with another Pokemon like Whimsicott to set Tailwind.

  • Mega Evolving Staraptor: Delaying Mega Evolution can preserve Intimidate to weaken physical attackers like Garchomp and Basculegion-M. It can also preserve Staraptor's Normal typing, keeping it immune to Last Respects from Basculegion-M and Rage Fist from Annihilape. This allows Staraptor to switch into a high-Base Power attack, saving a teammate while weakening Basculegion-M with Intimidate. It can use Protect to scout what a Choice Scarf Basculegion-M locks itself into and delay Mega Evolution if Basculegion-M uses Last Respects.

Other Options

  • Dual Wingbeat: Dual Wingbeat can be used over Brave Bird to OHKO Sneasler and Whimsicott through a Focus Sash. Mega Staraptor loses its ability to OHKO Basculegion-M with Brave Bird at +1 Attack if it runs Dual Wingbeat.

SP Spreads

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Jolly or Adamant: A Jolly nature will ensure Mega Staraptor outspeeds metagame staples like Garchomp, Mega Charizard Y, and Mega Floette while granting a Speed tie with other Mega Staraptor. An Adamant nature can be used in combination with Tickle or Charm from Whimsicott, allowing Mega Staraptor's Close Combat to OHKO bulkier variants of Garchomp or Archaludon with one or more Defense boosts.

  • 32 HP / 9 SpD / 25 Spe with Adamant: The Special Defense and HP investment allow Mega Staraptor to always survive Electro Shot from Archaludon at +1 Special Defense. The Speed investment allows it to outrun Modest Mega Floette. An Adamant nature allows it to OHKO Basculegion-M at +1 Attack with Brave Bird.

Teambuilding

  • Fairy-type Weaknesses: Mega Floette and Sylveon threaten to OHKO the less bulky Mega Staraptor set with Moonblast or Hyper Beam, respectively, even at +1 Special Defense. These Pokemon are also not good targets for Close Combat, making it hard for the bulkier set to boost its defense before being hit by a strong Fairy-type move.

  • Other Weaknesses: Gholdengo shrugs off both of Mega Staraptor's STAB attacks and can set up Nasty Plot to try getting an OHKO with Make It Rain or Shadow Ball before Mega Staraptor can use Close Combat or Roost. Mega Raichu Y outspeeds and threatens an OHKO with Zap Cannon, and even if Zap Cannon does not OHKO, the paralysis will make it easier for its teammates to finish Mega Staraptor off. Mega Froslass threatens heavy damage or an OHKO that cannot be redirected with Blizzard, is immune to Close Combat, and boosts its Defense with Snow Warning to survive Brave Bird.

  • Soft Counters: Mega Mawile and Mega Metagross threaten an OHKO with Play Rough or Psychic Fangs, respectively. Mega Mawile in particular is often on Trick Room teams to use Mega Staraptor's Speed against it and can have Hyper Cutter before Mega Evolving to ignore Intimidate. The Mega Metagross matchup is playable with support like Charm from Whimsicott, and Rage Powder and Trick Room reversal from Sinistcha help versus Mega Mawile, but these matchups are still threatening.

  • Perish Trap: Mega Gengar's Perish Song in combination with its Shadow Tag ability can deal with Mega Staraptor before it can ramp up its stat boosts. Mega Gengar's teammates like Incineroar and Maushold can use Fake Out to prevent Whimsicott from boosting Mega Staraptor, or Maushold can redirect Charm with Follow Me. Vivillon can shut down Mega Staraptor with Sleep Powder and save Mega Gengar with Rage Powder. This strategy ignores Mega Staraptor's ability to increase its bulk and can counter a slower setup playstyle.

  • Support Partners: Whimsicott has moves like Charm and Fake Tears to let Mega Staraptor flip its matchups against Mega Floette and Sylveon by making it strong enough to OHKO bulkier variants or making it bulky enough to survive their hits if Close Combat cannot do so. Its Tailwind increases the chance Mega Staraptor will get to use Close Combat to increase its bulk before a foe attacks. Sinistcha increases longevity and offsets Brave Bird recoil with Hospitality and Life Dew and redirects threatening attacks like Mega Raichu Y's Zap Cannon and Archaludon's Electro Shot. Mega Staraptor handles Incineroar and Kingambit in return with Close Combat. Grimmsnarl makes Mega Staraptor even harder to KO with Reflect and Light Screen, allowing Mega Staraptor to always survive Archaludon's Electro Shot with Light Screen up. It can also quickly boost Mega Staraptor's Attack with Parting Shot. The bulky spread works best with these partners that can boost Mega Staraptor's Attack.

  • Offensive Partners: Garchomp can freely use Earthquake next to Mega Staraptor, hitting threats like Gholdengo and Mega Raichu Y. Choice Scarf Basculegion-M can outspeed and OHKO Mega Raichu Y with Wave Crash or 150-Base Power Last Respects and Gholdengo, Mega Froslass, or Mega Metagross with 100-Base Power Last Respects. Gholdengo handles Fairy-types with Make It Rain, ignores Perish Song, and threatens to OHKO Mega Gengar with Shadow Ball.Mega Staraptor handles Incineroar and Kingambit for Gholdengo and Basculegion-M.

  • Alternative Mega Evolutions: Fire-types like Mega Delphox and Mega Charizard Y have a better matchup against Fairy-types, Steel-types, and Mega Froslass. Mega Delphox in particular is strong against Mega Gengar. Mega Staraptor, in turn, is a better choice against Rock-types like Mega Tyranitar and Hisuian Arcanine and in the rain matchup. Mega Raichu Y can be a stronger choice against opposing Mega Staraptor to avoid possible Speed ties. It can also be brought to a battle alongside Mega Staraptor to use Lightning Rod to save Mega Staraptor from opposing Mega Raichu Y's Zap Cannon. Mega Staraptor, in turn, is a better choice against Mega Raichu Y's counters: Garchomp and Sinistcha.

Fast Attacker.description:
• Garchomp, thanks to its strong offense, good coverage against the current format's major threats, and nice Speed tier, cements itself as a top threat in Regulation M-B, offensively checking the likes of Mega Charizard Y, Sneasler, Incineroar, and Kingambit with ease.

  • Rock Slide: Rock Slide allows Garchomp to threaten Flying-type Pokemon, namely Mega Charizard Y and Mega Aerodactyl. It can also deal considerable damage to Mega Delphox and is Garchomp's only way to hit Whimsicott, which are immune to Earthquake and resist it, respectively. Rock Slide, thanks to Garchomp's high Speed, can be used to fish for flinches, though it is generally an unreliable path to victory.

  • Life Orb: Life Orb allows Garchomp to always OHKO Mega Charizard Y with Rock Slide and OHKO opposing Garchomp with Dragon Claw.

  • Rough Skin: Rough Skin allows Garchomp to punish Fake Out from the likes of Sneasler and Incineroar, while also breaking the Focus Sash of physical attackers such as Kingambit, Sneasler, and Basculegion-M.

Other Options

  • Stomping Tantrum: Stomping Tantrum can be run on teams that don't have many Earthquake-immune Pokemon, allowing Garchomp to deal consistent Ground-type damage without threatening its partners. This comes at the cost of either Earthquake or Rock Slide, either limiting Garchomp's offensive capabilities or preventing it from OHKOing Mega Charizard Y.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Ice-type Pokemon like Mega Froslass and Alolan Ninetales threaten big damage with Blizzard and can lessen Garchomp's damage output with Aurora Veil. Pokemon that commonly run Ice-type coverage, like Mega Metagross and Mega Swampert, also cause issues, as both can outspeed Garchomp — whether it be naturally or through Swift Swim — and OHKO it with Ice Punch, while Mega Swampert is also bulky enough to tank two Dragon Claws. Mega Aerodactyl can do similarly with Ice Fang.

  • Fairy-type Pokemon like Mega Floette and Sylveon threaten Garchomp with Moonblast and Hyper Voice, while Mega Floette has the chance to Speed tie with Garchomp. Whimsicott in particular is problematic, as it is also resistant to Ground-type attacks and can use Tailwind to allow Pokemon that Garchomp usually outspeeds, like Sylveon and most Mega Floette, to KO it before it can move.

  • Mega Scovillain provides issues for Garchomp, easily redirecting its attacks and burning it. Incineroar can also weaken Garchomp with Intimidate, while Fake Out significantly hinders Garchomp's potential momentum.

  • Opposing Dragon-type Pokemon like Choice Scarf Hydreigon and Mega Dragonite can either outspeed Garchomp or withstand it for a turn and OHKO it with Draco Meteor or Dragon Pulse, respectively.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Charizard Y is immune to Garchomp's Earthquake and pressures Ice- and Fairy-type Pokemon with Weather Ball, OHKOing the Ice-type Pokemon and outdamaging the Fairy-types. Mega Charizard Y also threatens Mega Metagross with Weather Ball or Heat Wave and, when the sun is up, Mega Swampert with Solar Beam. Mega Charizard Y can also pressure Mega Scovillain without fear of being burnt. Garchomp, in return, hits the many Rock-type Pokemon that threaten Mega Charizard Y, like Mega Tyranitar and Glimmora, with Earthquake while also threatening opposing Mega Charizard Y with Rock Slide.

  • Whimsicott provides Tailwind, allowing Garchomp to outspeed other Garchomp as well as Hydreigon and threaten to OHKO them with Dragon Claw. Moonblast can also be used to threaten Dragon-type Pokemon, as a double target with Moonblast and Dragon Claw OHKOes Mega Dragonite. In return, Garchomp pressures the likes of Gholdengo and Kingambit, which would otherwise threaten Whimsicott with Make It Rain and Iron Head, respectively.

  • Kingambit threatens Ice- and Fairy-type Pokemon with Iron Head, while both it and Basculegion-M threaten Incineroar with Low Kick and Wave Crash, respectively.

Bulky Attacker.description:
• Bulky Garchomp utilizes its high Speed and Attack in conjunction with defensive items to become an all-rounder that can be brought to almost any matchup, with coverage to threaten top Pokemon like Sneasler, Mega Charizard Y, opposing Garchomp, and sometimes even Mega Floette.

  • Rock Slide vs Stomping Tantrum: Rock Slide allows Garchomp to fish for flinches and threaten Mega Charizard Y with serious damage. Stomping Tantrum, on the other hand, offers a secondary, single-target Ground-type STAB option, bypassing Wide Guard from Aegislash and Aerodactyl and giving Garchomp the ability to threaten Ground-type damage without also threatening its partner with Earthquake.

  • Protect vs Poison Jab: Protect is an amazing tool for any team, allowing Garchomp to defensively position itself throughout the game. Poison Jab can be run to threaten Fairy-types, namely Mega Floette, Sylveon, and Whimsicott; it is only run on Garchomp sets with Roseli Berry, because Poison Jab commonly misses OHKOs and Roseli Berry lets Garchomp take a Fairy-type attack before finishing the job with another Poison Jab.

Other Options

  • Rock Tomb: Rock Tomb, similar to Rock Slide, provides coverage against Mega Charizard Y but avoids Wide Guard from the likes of Aerodactyl. It also provides a form of Speed control but is really only useful against Mega Charizard Y because of its inability to fish for flinches or damage both foes.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry grants Garchomp far more longevity by allowing it to avoid 2HKOs from attacks such as Close Combat from Sneasler.

  • Roseli Berry: Roseli Berry allows Garchomp to take on the format's Fairy-types when used in combination with Poison Jab in one-on-one scenarios.

Abilities

  • Rough Skin: Rough Skin punishes attacks like Close Combat and Liquidation from Sneasler and Basculegion-M, respectively, breaking their Focus Sashes. It also punishes Fake Out from Incineroar; at low HP, Incineroar often cannot afford to use Fake Out on Garchomp without KOing itself.

SP Spreads

  • 19 HP / 26 Atk / 21 Spe with Jolly: The Attack investment allows Garchomp to OHKO uninvested Mega Charizard Y with Rock Slide, while the Speed investment lets it outrun maximum Speed Hisuian Arcanine. The bulk allows Garchomp to almost always survive Last Respects from Basculegion-M after two of its allies have fainted and always survive Knock Off from Jolly Mega Tyranitar after a Dragon Dance.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Even with Roseli Berry, Garchomp can struggle against Fairy-types, as Poison Jab doesn't OHKO them, leaving Garchomp vulnerable to being OHKOed by Mega Floette's Light of Ruin and Sylveon's Hyper Beam. Garchomp also struggles to damage Mega Froslass, which can OHKO it with Blizzard. Opposing Dragon-types like Mega Dragonite, Archaludon, and Hydreigon can be issues for Garchomp, as they can survive Dragon Claw or Earthquake and retaliate with Draco Meteor. Without an offensive item like Soft Sand, Garchomp may also struggle to deal damage to the likes of Incineroar and Mega Scovillain, especially after being affected by Intimidate or a burn, respectively.

Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Charizard Y is a great partner for Garchomp, resisting the Fairy-type attacks that threaten Garchomp, OHKOing Mega Froslass and Alolan Ninetales, and, when the two are next to each other, allowing Garchomp to use Earthquake freely. Fairy-type partners like Whimsicott and Mega Floette can threaten opposing Dragon-types, while partners like Mega and base Glimmora and as well as Sneasler can threaten opposing Fairy-types.

  • How to Overcome Garchomp's Weaknesses: Keeping Garchomp in the back and removing threats to it early on are good ideas, as its amazing coverage lets it easily clean up a lot of the format's common Pokemon. Having switch-ins to Fairy-types is also a must, as they pose a huge threat to Garchomp even with Roseli Berry. Garchomp also appreciates allies that can stay on the field alongside it while it continuously deals damage with Earthquake, such as Mega Aerodactyl, which can provide Tailwind, use Rock Slide to hit opposing Flying-types, and use Dual Wingbeat to weaken and threaten Sinistcha, a Pokemon Garchomp can struggle to hit.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Choice Scarf Garchomp is able to leverage its high offensive stats, good typing, and coverage to become a versatile threat fit for many teams; thanks to its Choice Scarf, it can outspeed and deal heavy damage to otherwise faster Pokemon like Mega Gengar and Sneasler.

  • Earthquake and Stomping Tantrum: Earthquake gives Garchomp a strong spread damage option, while Stomping Tantrum offers single-target Ground-type damage when trying to avoid Wide Guard or when positioned next to a Pokemon that is not immune to Earthquake. Knowing when to pick either one is vital, as locking into Earthquake when Garchomp's partner cannot safely take it can lose the game; alternatively, locking into Stomping Tantrum against redirection from the likes of Sinistcha and Vivillon can render Garchomp nearly useless.

  • Rock Slide: Rock Slide allows Garchomp to OHKO or deal heavy damage to Mega Charizard Y. Thanks to Choice Scarf, Garchomp can fish for flinches against fast Pokemon like Choice Scarf Basculegion-M and Mega Delphox, a role Garchomp without Choice Scarf is incapable of fulfilling.

Other Options

  • Rock Tomb: Rock Tomb is an alternative to Rock Slide, offering speed control and still offering a way to hit Mega Charizard Y hard. It loses the ability to cause flinches and deal spread damage, however.

Items

  • Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf allows Garchomp to outrun faster foes such as Mega Froslass and Aerodactyl, allowing it to revenge kill the aforementioned foes before they threaten it with Blizzard or set up Tailwind, respectively.

Abilities

  • Rough Skin: Rough Skin punishes Fake Out from foes like Incineroar and Sneasler, providing chip damage and, in Sneasler's case, potentially breaking its Focus Sash.

SP Spreads

  • 29 Atk / 15 SpD / 22 Spe with Adamant: The SPs invested in Special Defense allow Garchomp to survive Dazzling Gleam from Timid Mega Floette, while the Speed investment lets Garchomp outspeed Choice Scarf Basculegion-M when holding a Choice Scarf of its own. The remaining SPs are invested in Attack.

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant: This spread opts for more Speed and power, ensuring that Garchomp at least Speed ties other Choice Scarf Garchomp, outspeeds Choice Scarf Rotom-Wash and Mega Aerodactyl, and deals as much damage as possible.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Fairy-types like Mega Floette, Sylveon, Mega Gardevoir, and Whimsicott all threaten Garchomp with OHKOs or 2HKOs from their Fairy-type STAB attacks while also boasting an immunity to Dragon Claw, easily taking advantage of Garchomp's inability to switch moves. Whimsicott in particular also resists Garchomp's Ground-type STAB attacks and can use Tailwind to allow partners like Mega Floette to outspeed and OHKO Garchomp with Moonblast. Mega Froslass is able to easily OHKO Garchomp with Blizzard, while Fake Out from Sneasler and Incineroar can take advantage of Garchomp's inability to use Protect, leaving it vulnerable to attacks such as Draco Meteor from Hydreigon and Archaludon. Hydreigon and Mega Dragonite can easily take advantage when Garchomp locks into a Ground-type move, threatening it with Draco Meteor and Dragon Pulse, respectively, while Archaludon and opposing Garchomp are able to switch in on Rock Slide and threaten Garchomp with Draco Meteor and Dragon Claw, respectively. Rotom-Wash can also easily take attacks from Garchomp while threatening to burn it with Will-O-Wisp, and Mega Scovillain is able to redirect Garchomp's attacks, burning it in the process. Sinistcha and Farigiraf can set up Trick Room right in front of Garchomp, turning the Speed boost from Choice Scarf into a hindrance. Corviknight resists or, in the case of Ground-type attacks, is immune to all of Garchomp's STAB options, can shrug off Rock Slide, and can either set up Tailwind or use Bulk Up in the face of Garchomp, setting up an ally for success or turning itself into a win condition, respectively.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Charizard Y is able to sit next to Garchomp while it freely uses Earthquake and make Blizzard from Mega Froslass and Alolan Ninetales inaccurate by setting sun. Additionally, it is able to resist Fairy-type attacks and fire back with Weather Ball and Heat Wave while threatening to OHKO Mega Froslass and Sinistcha with the same moves. Incineroar also threatens Mega Froslass and Sinistcha and can safely switch into their attacks while using Fake Out against foes like Hydreigon to keep Garchomp safe for another turn or Parting Shot to safely bring in Garchomp. In return, Garchomp is able to threaten Rock-types like Mega Tyranitar and Lycanroc-D and deal with opposing non-Choice Scarf Garchomp. Mega Froslass, Sinistcha, and Farigiraf are all threatened by Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave; Fairy-types fear Iron Head; and Hydreigon and Archaludon take solid damage from Low Kick. Kingambit appreciates Garchomp's positive matchup against Mega Charizard Y and Sneasler. Mega Floette is able to threaten the Dragon-types Garchomp fears with heavy damage, as well as easily take out Rotom-Wash and take attacks from Mega Froslass before retaliating with Moonblast or Light of Ruin. Mega Aerodactyl deals heavy damage to Sinistcha with Dual Wingbeat, deterring it from attempting to redirect Garchomp's attacks; Mega Aerodactyl is also capable of using Ice Fang to OHKO opposing Garchomp.

  • How to Overcome Garchomp's Weaknesses: Bringing Choice Scarf Garchomp alongside offensive threats that complement it well, such as Mega Charizard Y, is a must to ensure it isn't easily stopped by Pokemon that resist or are immune to whatever move it has decided to lock into. When teambuilding, placing Garchomp on a team with Fairy-, Dragon-, and Ice-type damage is preferred, though not necessary thanks to Garchomp's flexibility, as it often functions as glue for teams. Mega Charizard Y threatens the Fairy- and Ice-type Pokemon that scare away Garchomp and, more importantly, appreciates Garchomp's ability to threaten opposing Mega Charizard Y and Dragon-types with Rock Slide and Dragon Claw, respectively. Mega Floette and Sylveon appreciate Garchomp's Ground-type attacks threatening Kingambit and Sneasler and, in return, provide coverage against problematic Dragon-types like Mega Dragonite. Kingambit and Mega Aerodactyl perform similar roles against Ice-types and other foes that trouble Garchomp, appreciating the wide array of coverage Garchomp has at its disposal to dispatch nearly any Pokemon. Kingambit has the added benefit of deterring Trick Room from Sinistcha and Farigiraf thanks to its naturally low Speed and can hit them hard with Kowtow Cleave.

Aurora Veil Setter.description:
• Mega Froslass uses its excellent Speed, Fake Out immunity, and Snow Warning to reliably set Aurora Veil for offensive teams without being too passive, using an accurate Blizzard in snow to pressure both foes and potentially freeze them while using Shadow Ball to threaten a metagame staple in Basculegion-M. This makes Mega Froslass a strong fit on offensive teams that can use Aurora Veil to stomach attacks and trade more aggressively.

  • Aurora Veil: Aurora Veil is Mega Froslass's main selling point, making it much harder for foes to remove it and its ally. This is especially valuable for teammates such as Sneasler, Kingambit, Basculegion-M, Garchomp, Hisuian Arcanine, and Kommo-o that appreciate the extra bulk when forcing trades, setting up, or staying on the field to keep offensive pressure. Aurora Veil can also make bulkier partners like Corviknight much harder to break through, but Mega Froslass gains more value by supporting aggressive teams rather than passive teammates.

  • Modest versus Timid: A Modest nature is preferred for the extra damage output, notably guaranteeing an OHKO on Basculegion-M with Shadow Ball while still allowing Froslass to outspeed major threats such as Garchomp, Mega Floette, Mega Charizard Y, and Mega Dragonite as well as Speed tie Adamant Sneasler. A Timid nature can be used instead to Speed tie Jolly Sneasler while outspeeding Maushold and opposing Modest Mega Froslass, but the loss in power is noticeable.

  • Mega Evolving Froslass: Mega Froslass can forgo immediately Mega Evolving to ensure snow is active on the turn it uses Aurora Veil if the opponent has a slower weather setter like Mega Charizard Y, Pelipper, or Tyranitar. Staying in base forme can also give Cursed Body a chance to punish moves like Mega Aerodactyl's Rock Slide while Froslass positions to Mega Evolve and set snow later.

Other Options

  • Rain Dance: Rain Dance can be used over Shadow Ball to give Mega Froslass additional defensive utility against Mega Charizard Y and Torkoal while allowing Archaludon to use Electro Shot, but it removes Mega Froslass's own snow, making Aurora Veil unusable.

Abilities

  • Snow Warning: Snow Warning enables Mega Froslass to use Aurora Veil and makes Blizzard a perfectly accurate spread STAB attack against targets such as Garchomp, Whimsicott, Mega Dragonite, and Aerodactyl. Snow also boosts Mega Froslass's Defense, helping it helps Froslass take physical attacks like Rock Slide from Aerodactyl and Knock Off from Tyranitar more comfortably while trying to set Aurora Veil. Snow Warning also lets Mega Froslass contest weather from opposing setters such as Mega Charizard Y, Pelipper, and Mega Tyranitar if Mega Evolution is timed correctly.

SP Spreads

  • 30 HP / 21 Def / 15 Spe with Timid: This bulkier spread still outspeeds Garchomp, Mega Floette, Mega Charizard Y, and Mega Dragonite while giving Mega Froslass much better physical bulk with snow active. With Aurora Veil up, Aerodactyl's Rock Slide becomes a 4HKO, while Incineroar's Flare Blitz and Aegislash's Poltergeist become guaranteed 3HKOs, and even a 200-Base Power Last Respects from Basculegion-M fails to OHKO Froslass. Even without Special Attack investment, Mega Froslass still 2HKOes Archaludon with Blizzard and OHKOes uninvested Mega Gengar with Shadow Ball while heavily pressuring Garchomp and Dragonite.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Mega Froslass struggles most against Pokemon that either remove snow or threaten it before it can set Aurora Veil. Mega Charizard Y removes snow with Drought and threatens heavy spread damage with Heat Wave, while Mega Tyranitar overwrites snow with sand and pressures Mega Froslass with Rock- and Dark-type attacks. Hisuian Arcanine is especially dangerous because Head Smash and Flare Blitz can OHKO even bulkier Mega Froslass through snow's Defense boost and Aurora Veil. Kingambit and Incineroar also pressure Mega Froslass directly while walling its STAB attacks and threatening it back with their own STAB moves, making it difficult for Mega Froslass to do much beyond setting Aurora Veil. Kingambit is especially troublesome, as Sucker Punch can pick off Mega Froslass once it has been weakened, while Incineroar disrupts Mega Froslass's physical partners with Intimidate. Archaludon can take Blizzard well and retaliate with Flash Cannon, and Aerodactyl can outspeed Mega Froslass and threaten it with Rock Slide.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Froslass fits best with offensive teammates that can use Aurora Veil to stay on the field longer and force trades more aggressively. Sneasler is one of Froslass's best partners, using Fake Out to protect itself while Aurora Veil is being set and Close Combat to threaten Kingambit, Incineroar, and Mega Tyranitar. Kingambit appreciates Aurora Veil making it harder to remove while setting up Swords Dance or trading with faster teams. It threatens Ghost-types that pressure Mega Froslass, using Kowtow Cleave for consistent damage against Aegislash and Farigiraf as well as Sucker Punch to pick off faster threats such as Mega Gengar and opposing Basculegion-M once they are in range. Garchomp appreciates Aurora Veil giving it more room to attack, using Earthquake to threaten Steel-, Fire-, and Rock-types such as Kingambit, Archaludon, Incineroar, Hisuian Arcanine, and Mega Tyranitar. Rock Slide also lets Garchomp pressure Mega Charizard Y and Hisuian Arcanine while giving it a spread move that can punish both foes. Hisuian Arcanine gives Mega Froslass teams immediate pressure against opposing Fire-types like Mega Charizard Y with Head Smash and Rock Slide while threatening Steel-types such as Kingambit with Flare Blitz. Whimsicott provides Tailwind and Encore, letting Mega Froslass's offensive teammates overwhelm faster teams while punishing Protect, Fake Out, and setup attempts. Kommo-o can use Aurora Veil to set up more safely and pressure Kingambit, Incineroar, and Archaludon with Aura Sphere. Basculegion-M uses Aurora Veil to survive revenge killing attempts from priority users like Kingambit's Sucker Punch and Aeiglash's Shadow Sneak as well as faster attackers like Mega Gengar while pressuring Fire- and Rock-types such as Mega Charizard Y, Incineroar, Hisuian Arcanine, and Mega Tyranitar. Archaludon can fit on Rain Dance variants with Politoed and Basculegion-M, as Mega Froslass can support it with Aurora Veil and set rain later on in the game. Aurora Veil makes Archaludon even harder to remove, while Rain Dance lets it use Electro Shot consistently to threaten targets such as Mega Floette and Mega Charizard Y.

  • How to Overcome Mega Froslass's Weaknesses: Against opposing weather teams, avoid Mega Evolving early if the opponent can still overwrite snow with Pokemon such as Mega Charizard Y, Mega Tyranitar, and Pelipper. Against Kingambit and Incineroar, pair Mega Froslass with teammates such as Sneasler, Garchomp, Basculegion-M, and Hisuian Arcanine that can immediately threaten them instead of letting them attack freely. Against faster Rock Slide users such as opposing Aerodactyl, use Protect and Tailwind support from Whimsicott or Wide Guard from partners such as Aerodactyl to stop Mega Froslass from being flinched before it can set Aurora Veil.

Bulky Support.description:
• Rotom-Wash is able to leverage its great bulk and defensive typing alongside healing items to become very difficult for the opponent to remove from the field, using Will-O-Wisp against the many physical attackers in the format such as Garchomp and Kingambit while being able to deal good damage to staples like Basculegion-M and Incineroar.

  • Hydro Pump: Hydro Pump is Rotom-Wash's only option for Water-type STAB, enabling it to handle Ground-types, namely Garchomp, while also hitting Incineroar.

  • Will-O-Wisp: Will-O-Wisp allows Rotom-Wash to beat Kingambit and physical attackers like Mega Tyranitar; after burn damage, Hydro Pump will always 2HKO Garchomp.

Other Options

  • Volt Switch: Volt Switch allows Rotom-Wash to play as a slow, bulky pivot, similarly to Incineroar. This does, however, come at the cost of Rotom-Wash losing either reliable Electric-type STAB in Thunderbolt or Protect.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry grants Rotom-Wash solid healing, allowing it to avoid 2HKOs from Sneasler's Close Combat and Sylveon's Hyper Voice.

  • Leftovers: Leftovers provides Rotom-Wash with more consistent recovery, though it requires Rotom-Wash to stay on the field longer to provide good value; it also allows Rotom-Wash to always avoid a 2HKO from Glimmora's Sludge Bomb.

Abilities

  • Levitate: Levitate not only allows Rotom-Wash to be a good ally for Garchomp, letting Garchomp use Earthquake without fear of damaging its partner, but also allows Rotom-Wash to switch in on opposing Garchomp rather freely.

SP Spreads

  • 31 HP / 12 Def / 1 SpA / 20 SpD / 2 Spe with Bold: With the given bulk, Rotom-Wash survives Solar Beam from Timid Mega Charizard Y and Sucker Punch from +2 Black Glasses Kingambit while having a chance to survive Last Respects from Adamant Basculegion-M after two of Basculegion-M's allies have fainted. The HP SPs give Rotom-Wash an even HP stat to optimize Sitrus Berry recovery. The Speed investment allows Rotom-Wash to outspeed Jolly Choice Scarf Basculegion-M under Tailwind, and the remaining SP is invested in Special Attack.

  • 31 HP / 14 Def / 16 SpA / 3 SpD / 2 Spe with Modest: This spread is more offensively oriented, allowing Rotom-Wash to guarantee a 2HKO on minimum-bulk Garchomp with Hydro Pump and avoid a 2HKO from Garchomp's Dragon Claw; it also survives Kowtow Cleave from +1 Kingambit, such as after an Intimidate. The same Speed benchmark as above is reached, and the remaining SPs are invested in Special Defense.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Choice Scarf Rotom-Wash trades most of its bulk investment for greater offensive investment, while still being able to tank hits thanks to its naturally high defensive stats. With Choice Scarf, Rotom-Wash can more consistently take on the likes of Aerodactyl, Mega Delphox, and Choice Scarf Basculegion-M.

  • Electroweb: Thanks to Choice Scarf, Rotom-Wash can consistently use Electroweb to provide Speed control for its team, slowing down fast threats like Aerodactyl and Alolan Ninetales.

  • Volt Switch: As opposed to the bulkier sets, Choice Scarf Rotom-Wash can use Volt Switch to quickly pivot out of unfavorable situations while dealing chip damage, possibly breaking a Focus Sash on a Sneasler, Basculegion-M, Aerodactyl, or Whimsicott.

Other Options

  • Will-O-Wisp: Will-O-Wisp can cripple physical attackers and, with Choice Scarf, be used on fast Pokemon like Sneasler before they move. It is generally forgone, however, as locking Rotom-Wash into a status move is undesirable. Running Will-O-Wisp also requires dropping Thunderbolt, Rotom-Wash's most consistent Electric-type STAB option.

Items

  • Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf allows Rotom-Wash to outrun faster Pokemon such as Talonflame, Mega Charizard Y, and Mega Gengar. Thanks to the Speed boost from Choice Scarf, Rotom-Wash becomes a reliable revenge killer, switching in to take out low-HP Pokemon with either Electroweb, which also hits the other foe and provides Speed control, or Volt Switch, which improves positioning.

SP Spreads

  • 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Modest: This spread maximizes Rotom-Wash's Speed and Special Attack, allowing it to outpace the likes of Mega Delphox and Adamant Mega Aerodactyl.

  • 14 HP / 27 SpA / 25 Spe with Timid: With the given Speed investment, Choice Scarf Rotom-Wash always outruns Choice Scarf (RC) Basculegion-M while surviving Moonblast from Timid Mega Floette; the remaining SPs are invested in Special Attack.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: While Rotom-Wash has an amazing defensive typing, it struggles against Grass-types, mainly Sinistcha and Mega Venusaur, which resist all of its common attacks. Sinistcha can also redirect these attacks, preventing Rotom-Wash from dealing meaningful damage or burning foes like Kingambit, while Sinistcha and Mega Venusaur can heavily damage Rotom-Wash with Matcha Gotcha and Giga Drain, respectively. Dragon-types like Archaludon and Hydreigon can also shrug off a burn, resist all of Rotom-Wash's common attacks, and retaliate with Electro Shot and Dark Pulse, respectively. Mega Floette and Mega Scovillain pose issues for Rotom-Wash as well, setting up in front of it or heavily damaging it with Giga Drain, respectively; Mega Floette can easily take Rotom-Wash's attacks thanks to its naturally high Special Defense and retaliate with Moonblast or Light of Ruin, with the latter threatening an OHKO.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Garchomp works well with Rotom-Wash, freely using Earthquake and threatening opposing Dragon-types with Dragon Claw. Excadrill can also use Earthquake next to Rotom-Wash, as well as Iron Head to beat Mega Floette and Rock Slide to hit Mega Charizard Y, which can threaten to OHKO Rotom-Wash with Solar Beam. Corviknight is another great ally that threatens Sinistcha and Mega Floette, while Mega Tyranitar can deal heavy damage across the board to offset Rotom-Wash's passivity and appreciates Rotom-Wash's ability to threaten Basculegion-M. In return, Mega Tyranitar threatens Mega Charizard Y and Sinistcha, both of which boast Grass-type attacks that threaten Rotom-Wash. When building with Rotom-Wash and Mega Tyranitar, however, it is important to keep in mind that they share a weakness to Mega Floette. To counteract this, the aforementioned Steel-types, Excadrill and Corviknight, can be used to take down Mega Floette.

  • How to Overcome Rotom-Wash's Weaknesses: Bringing safe switch-ins to attacks that target Rotom-Wash's weaknesses is recommended; Pokemon like Corviknight work well in this role. Offensive Pokemon like Excadrill and Garchomp work well alongside Rotom-Wash, combining Earthquake with Hydro Pump or Electric-type moves to deal solid damage. Playing Rotom-Wash as a supporting pivot is best, burning foes or providing Speed control and chip damage throughout the game.

Sand Sweeper.description:
• Excadrill is a staple of sand teams due to its ability and STAB combination allowing it to outspeed the metagame and threaten common threats to its sand-setting partner, Mega Tyranitar, including Sneasler, Archaludon, Mega Floette, and Sylveon.

  • Earthquake versus High Horsepower: Earthquake gives Excadrill an incredibly powerful spread move; however, it can't be safely used next to partners without a Ground immunity and makes Excadrill susceptible to Wide Guard. High Horsepower can be safely used next to any partner, but it comes at the cost of Excadrill's ability to deal big spread damage and leaves Excadrill more susceptible to redirection.

  • Rock Slide: Rock Slide gives Excadrill an option to hit Mega Charizard Y for big damage and works as an alternative spread option that doesn't hit partners. Excadrill can also effectively fish for flinches with Rock Slide due to its high Speed in sand.

Items

  • Focus Sash: The extra survivability given by Focus Sash is necessary to let Excadrill fire off more attacks before being KOed. Focus Sash lets Sand Rush-boosted Excadrill 2HKO Choice Scarf Basculegion-M while surviving Wave Crash; it also allows Excadrill to tank a Close Combat from Unburden-boosted Sneasler deal an OHKO in return with Earthquake or High Horsepower.

Abilities

  • Sand Rush: While sand is active, Sand Rush allows Excadrill to outspeed every Pokemon in the metagame besides Sneasler with an Unburden boost.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Without sand, Excadrill is relatively slow, allowing Pokemon like Choice Scarf Basculegion-M, Sneasler, and Mega Charizard Y to outspeed and threaten it if sand is stalled out or overwritten by another weather. Excadrill commonly wants to be led alongside Tyranitar to activate Sand Rush; however, this lead can be exploited because the two share weaknesses to Water-, Fighting-, and Ground-type moves. Garchomp can be a particularly bad matchup, since Rough Skin can break Excadrill's Focus Sash if Excadrill goes for Iron Head or High Horsepower, allowing Garchomp to OHKO it with Earthquake. Basculegion-M is another tough matchup, as non-Choice Scarf variants can bring Excadrill down to its Focus Sash with Wave Crash, tank an attack, and then KO it before it can move with Aqua Jet. Excadrill is unable to deal meaningful damage to both Corviknight and Rotom-Wash, and it's also susceptible to being burned and redirected by Mega Scovillain's Spicy Spray and Rage Powder, respectively.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Tyranitar is a must-have partner for Excadrill, since it sets up sand and threatens Mega Charizard Y and Basculegion-M with Rock Slide and Knock Off, respectively. Excadrill really appreciates Ground-immune partners because they can freely switch into Garchomp and let Excadrill use Earthquake with no drawback. Corviknight is excellent for this role; it effectively walls Garchomp, threatens Grass-types with Brave Bird, and can set up with Bulk Up while Excadrill puts on offensive pressure. Hydreigon and Rotom-Wash are other great options for Ground-immune partners. Hydreigon can offensively threaten Garchomp, Mega Scovillain, and Basculegion-M, while Rotom-Wash can threaten Water-types with Thunderbolt and physical attackers with Will-o-Wisp. Sinistcha can be a great partner, since it resists all the weaknesses that Excadrill and Mega Tyranitar share while providing redirection to protect Excadrill from attacks like Sneasler's Close Combat and Basculegion-M's Wave Crash.

  • How to Overcome Excadrill's Weaknesses: Mega Tyranitar and Excadrill should always be chosen together during Team Preview. Use Excadrill as an immediately deadly sweeper, especially to outspeed and OHKO Pokemon like Sneasler and Mega Floette that would otherwise be huge threats to Mega Tyranitar. Against opposing weather teams, time Tyranitar's Mega Evolution so that it can keep sand up, and position it well to keep it out of danger and preserve sand. Use the rest of the team to deal with threats to this duo, most importantly Garchomp, while keeping up offensive pressure.

Tailwind Support.description:
• Whimsicott is able to provide crucial Tailwind support to many Pokemon that rely on it, such as Mystic Water Basculegion-M, offensive Mega Floette, and bulky Garchomp. At the same time, it can shut down almost any attempts at setting up with Encore, making Whimsicott ideal for both support and disruption.

  • Encore: While Tailwind teams can sometimes struggle with setup Pokemon or moves such as Fake Out, Encore attaches a risk to these moves by forcing foes to switch out or prevent Encore in other ways risk being locked into a useless move. It synergizes well with Whimsicott's Grass typing, which allows it to ignore Rage Powder from Sinistcha attempting to redirect Encore. Encore can also be used to lock foes into resisted attacks, such as opposing Basculegion-M's Wave Crash instead of Last Respects, protecting Whimsicott and potentially its partner.

Items

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash allows Whimsicott to run more Speed but means it cannot be as offensive as Fairy Feather variants, as quite a few SPs are still required in bulk to survive Dual Wingbeat from Aerodactyl.

  • Fairy Feather: Fairy Feather allows Whimsicott to threaten a 2HKO on bulky Sitrus Berry Garchomp with Moonblast while leaving room for a lot of SPs in bulk. This item is mostly used when Focus Sash is used by a different Pokemon.

SP Spreads

  • 18 HP / 6 Def / 10 SpA / 32 Spe with Timid: This spread is only run by Focus Sash variants. Whimsicott will survive Dual Wingbeat from Jolly Aerodactyl almost the entire time, with the rest of the SPs prioritized towards Speed in order to Speed tie other Whimsicott.

  • 30 HP / 17 Def / 9 SpA / 10 SpD with Bold: This spread is only run by Fairy Feather variants, as Focus Sash variants do not need to hit as many benchmarks. Whimsicott is guaranteed to survive Iron Head from Adamant-natured Kingambit and will almost always survive Moonblast from Mega Floette. The offensive investment allows Whimsicott to almost always 2HKO bulky Sitrus Berry Garchomp.

  • 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Timid: When combined with Mega Floette's Fairy Aura, this SP spread allows Whimsicott to deal a large amount of damage. Whimsicott can afford to run this spread when holding Focus Sash, as Dual Wingbeat from Aerodactyl is the only attack it needs bulk to survive.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: While Whimsicott is almost never totally useless, as Encore will almost always achieve something, it struggles against Pokemon like Mega Charizard Y and Mega Delphox, as they usually don't mind being Encored and resist Moonblast from Whimsicott. Venusaur, in a similar vein, resists Moonblast and is not bothered by Encore too much. However, Moonblast can break Venusaur's Focus Sash, so attacking Venusaur can still be worthwhile. Additionally, Incineroar can pose problems for Whimsicott due to its immunity to Encore, that allows it to shrug off Moonblast, and access to Fake Out to stop Whimsicott from using Encore.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: While there are many Pokemon that appreciate Whimsicott's support and improve its performance in return, Mega Floette stands out as one of the best. Tailwind allows Mega Floette to outspeed nearly every other Pokemon barring other Tailwind-supported threats, while Fairy Aura allows Whimsicott to deal a surprisingly large amount of damage with Moonblast. Encore also helps Mega Floette beat foes it can struggle with, such as setup Corviknight and Aurora Veil Mega Froslass. Mega Charizard Y is another good partner, as Whimsicott's Tailwind lets even bulky variants outspeed Garchomp, one of Mega Charizard Y's biggest threats. Garchomp resists Weather Ball and Heat Wave, and Solar Beam isn't strong enough to take it out, but Whimsicott can bring Garchomp in range of Weather Ball with Moonblast. Garchomp itself is also a great partner, as it has a very good matchup against Mega Charizard Y and Mega Delphox, which Whimsicott struggles with.

  • How to Overcome Whimsicott's Weaknesses: When using Whimsicott, well-placed Encores can get its team out of many bad positions. Leveraging Whimsicott's presence on the field with Protect is also important for this, as the opponent may feel locked out of several moves while Whimsicott is present. Moves such as Aqua Jet and Aurora Veil, as well as Earth Power from Venusaur, are examples of options that require positioning around Encore. Certain moves are only used in specific situations, such as when Venusaur uses Earth Power against Glimmora or when Aqua Jet picks off a foe at low HP, while others, such as Protect, can render a Pokemon useless if it is forced to use them multiple turns in a row. As such, these moves require much more precise positioning when Whimsicott is on the field. Leveraging this pressure alongside Whimsicott's Protect and the opportunity cost of manually switching can exponentially increase Whimsicott's usefulness. The partners mentioned in the previous section can help cover Whimsicott's common switch-ins, with Garchomp beating Incineroar using Earthquake or Stomping Tantrum as well as Mega Delphox and Mega Charizard Y using Rock Slide. When facing opposing Tailwind teams, using defensive options such as an allied Incineroar or bulky Pokemon may be more consistent than attempting to win Speed ties against opposing Whimsicott and lock it into Tailwind.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Hydreigon finds its place in the metagame as an excellent Choice Scarf user, outspeeding and being a good answer to Choice Scarf Basculegion-M as well as other common Pokemon such as Garchomp, Sinistcha, Mega Froslass, Mega Delphox, and Mega Gengar. Hydreigon's typing is also helpful against Mega Charizard Y, allowing it to resist Heat Wave, sun-boosted Weather Ball, and Solar Beam while hitting it back hard with STAB Draco Meteor.

  • Earth Power vs. Heat Wave: Both Earth Power and Heat Wave can hit Steel-types, with Earth Power having the advantage of dealing more damage to Kingambit and Archaludon. On the other hand, Heat Wave being a spread move allows Hydreigon to hit Kingambit on teams that have redirection while also threatening Corviknight and Whimsicott.

  • Snarl: Snarl can weaken a plethora of special attackers, such as Mega Charizard Y, Mega Floette, Archaludon, Sylveon, and Mega Dragonite. After inducing a Special Attack drop, Hydreigon can always survive Mega Froslass's Blizzard as well as Archaludon's and Mega Dragonite's Dragon Pulse.

Items

  • Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf allows Hydreigon to always outspeed Choice Scarf Basculegion-M and Mega Aerodactyl.

Abilities

  • Levitate: Levitate provides Hydreigon with a helpful Ground immunity, making it a good partner for Pokemon that like spamming Earthquake like Excadrill.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Fairy-types like Mega Floette and Sylveon are the easiest and best way to keep Hydreigon in check, always OHKOing it with their STAB moves, while it can only slow them down with Special Attack drops from Snarl. After activating Unburden with White Herb or Focus Sash, Sneasler will always outspeed Hydreigon and OHKO it with Close Combat. Sneasler can also use Fake Out on Hydreigon, which is incredibly helpful for Sneasler's teammates like Garchomp and Basculegion-M, allowing Garchomp in particular to OHKO Hydreigon with Dragon Claw. Kingambit, Mega Tyranitar, and Corviknight are huge roadblocks for Choice Scarf Hydreigon: Kingambit and Mega Tyranitar can take any hit Hydreigon throws at them and retaliate with Low Kick or set up with Dragon Dance and Swords Dance. Alternatively, Corviknight can always survive a few Heat Waves and set up Tailwind.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Choice Scarf Hydreigon is a great piece on sand teams, as they appreciate its ability to threaten and potentially OHKO Choice Scarf Basculegion-M and most Garchomp sets, which they can struggle against. In return, Excadrill, a common feature on sand teams, threatens both Fairy- and Steel-types for Hydreigon with its STAB moves. Rotom-Wash also works well with Hydreigon, threatening damage on Corviknight as well as crippling Garchomp, Kingambit, and Mega Tyranitar with Will-O-Wisp. Mega Charizard Y is also a potential partner that appreciates Hydreigon threatening and removing Choice Scarf Basculegion-M and Garchomp while helping it in return by removing Steel-types, resisting Fairy-type attacks, hitting Fairy-types especially hard with sun-boosted Weather Ball, and cleanly removing Sneasler.

  • *How to Overcome Hydreigon's Weaknesses: Hydreigon appreciates partners that can threaten and deal huge damage to the Fairy- and Steel-types that wall it. Pokemon like Sneasler, Mega Charizard Y, Hisuian Arcanine, Corviknight, and Excadrill are all great against Fairy-types; some are also great against Kingambit and opposing Corviknight. Sneasler in particular is a good Hydreigon partner, hitting most Steel-types incredibly hard with Close Combat as well as having a great matchup against Fairy-types with Dire Claw or Gunk Shot. Mega Froslass and Corviknight have a great matchup against Sneasler, with Mega Froslass being immune to Close Combat and resisting Dire Claw while hitting Sneasler hard with either of its STAB moves. Corviknight is immune to Dire Claw and removes Sneasler with Brave Bird.

Glass Cannon.description:
• Mega Delphox serves as a solid offensive threat within the metagame, capable of outspeeding and removing the likes of Sinistcha, Sneasler, and Corviknight for its teammates while also making use of its good typing and high special bulk to directly combat opposing Mega threats such as Mega Gengar and Mega Froslass.

  • Psyshock vs. Psychic: Both of Mega Delphox's Psychic-type offensive moves have solid use cases: Psychic has higher overall damage, 2HKOing Garchomp and always OHKOing Sneasler and Kommo-o, while Psyshock enables Mega Delphox to remove Mega Floette and Sylveon with a guaranteed 2HKO on both.

  • Nasty Plot vs. Encore: Nasty Plot enables Mega Delphox to reach far higher damage thresholds, letting it score OHKOs it previously couldn't on foes like Sylveon and the Mega Charizard formes with its Psychic-type STAB moves and Corviknight with Heat Wave. This makes Mega Delphox a nightmare to position against and generally makes Nasty Plot the preferred option. However, Encore can lock threats such as Mega Floette, Garchomp, and Incineroar into moves such as Calm Mind, Protect, or Fake Out, enabling Mega Delphox or one of its teammates to safely eliminate them. Notably, Encore is far better than Nasty Plot late-game against Kingambit, as it can lock Kingambit into Sucker Punch, enabling Mega Delphox to stall out Sucker Punch's PP so Kingambit can be safely removed with Heat Wave.

SP Spreads

  • 5 HP / 32 SpA / 29 Spe with Timid: Mega Delphox's SP spread enables it to outspeed Mega Gengar while slightly increasing its bulk, giving it high odds of surviving Kingambit's non-Black Glasses-boosted Sucker Punch with Friend Guard support and always surviving Mega Aerodactyl's Rock Slide.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Mega Delphox struggles greatly to threaten Mega Tyranitar and Incineroar, which are able to shrug off its attacks and threaten it back with Dark-type STAB attacks like Knock Off and Throat Chop. Priority moves such as Kingambit's Sucker Punch and Aegislash's Shadow Sneak also prey on Mega Delphox's low physical bulk. Rain shuts Mega Delphox down by crippling its spread damage, and Mega Delphox struggles to handle many of rain's most common pieces like Archaludon and Basculegion-M. Basculegion-M especially proves challenging, as it is able to move before Mega Delphox and eliminate it with Mystic Water-boosted Aqua Jet or, with Choice Scarf, Wave Crash or Last Respects. Trick Room teams can turn Mega Delphox's incredible Speed against it, making it helpless against foes such as Mega Blastoise. Finally, priority Tailwind from Whimsicott and Talonflame can prove an annoyance for Mega Delphox, as it lets foes like Garchomp outspeed it and chip it down with Rock Slide before it can act.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Thanks to Levitate making Mega Delphox immune to Ground-type attacks, Garchomp can serve as an excellent partner, as it is capable of freely using Earthquake while also threatening the likes of Incineroar and Mega Tyranitar. In return, Mega Delphox can eliminate foes such as Sinistcha and Mega Froslass that pose a problem for Garchomp. Teammates like Sinistcha and Maushold can provide redirection support, drawing away attacks such as Kingambit's Sucker Punch. Sinistcha can also help Mega Delphox by combating Water-types like Milotic and Rotom-Wash through Matcha Gotcha. Maushold also serves well providing redirection against Ghost-type attacks from foes like Basculegion-M and Aegislash, enabling Mega Delphox to set up with Nasty Plot. Mega Floette serves as a strong alternative Mega Evolution for Mega Delphox, as it can come into matchups Mega Delphox struggles against, such as rain and Trick Room, to handle foes like Mega Dragonite, Mega Tyranitar, and Mega Blastoise. In return, Mega Delphox can prey on Poison-types that target Mega Floette, such as Mega Gengar and Glimmora. Incineroar provides Intimidate support, enabling Mega Delphox to stay in against foes like Garchomp and Basculegion-M, along with Fake Out pressure to help handle Focus Sash Glimmora. Vivillon can provide redirection support with Rage Powder, outspeed and put problematic threats such as Milotic and Aegislash to sleep, and provide Tailwind, enabling Mega Delphox to outspeed foes like Mega Aerodactyl and Choice Scarf Garchomp. Kingambit can pick off Basculegion-M and Aegislash for Mega Delphox while helping deal with Incineroar through Defiant and Low Kick, the latter of which also helps it deal with Mega Tyranitar.

  • How to Overcome Mega Delphox's Weaknesses: Mega Delphox relies on its partners to keep opposing physical attackers in check. Having redirection support on the field while it fires off its powerful STAB moves is vital to getting the most out of Mega Delphox. Garchomp alongside Mega Delphox creates a consistent vortex of high-power spread attacks that can be hard to position against, as Sinistcha doesn't want to enter on Mega Delphox's Heat Wave, while Incineroar and Mega Charizard Y hate entering on Earthquake and Rock Slide, respectively. If Mega Delphox finds itself out of position, it is usually safe enough to use Protect for a turn while a teammate repositions to take the heat off it. If necessary, Mega Delphox can make an aggressive play with its high special bulk, especially when bringing in Sinistcha.

Offensive Support.description:
• Talonflame can consistently set the pace of the battle due to the priority boost on Tailwind granted by Gale Wings. Gale Wings also gives it immediate offensive pressure with its primary STAB Flying-type moves. With its high Speed, Talonflame can threaten many prominent Pokemon like Kingambit, Sneasler, and Whimsicott with its STAB Fire- and Flying-type attacks.

  • Flare Blitz vs. Will-O-Wisp: Flare Blitz can threaten large damage onto Kingambit, Sinistcha, and Mega Froslass, while Will-O-Wisp provides damage reduction against physical attackers like Garchomp and Corviknight. Furthermore, Will-O-Wisp and Flare Blitz are Talonflame's only ways to pressure Kingambit and Aegislash.

  • Brave Bird vs. Dual Wingbeat vs. Acrobatics: Brave Bird, when boosted by Gale Wings, becomes a powerful priority attack, giving Talonflame immediate pressure. It is much stronger than Dual Wingbeat and Acrobatics, as only Brave Bird can OHKO Scovillain. However, Dual Wingbeat can also be valuable due to its ability to KO Pokemon such as Sneasler and Whimsicott through Focus Sash without breaking Gale Wings. Finally, the lack of recoil damage from Acrobatics allows no-item Talonflame to threaten heavy Flying-type damage without deactivating Gale Wings.

Other Options

  • Taunt: Taunt can be used over Flare Blitz or Will-O-Wisp for an extra tool against Trick Room teams. Furthermore, Taunt can be used to disrupt redirectors like Maushold and Sinistcha as well as setup Pokemon such as Calm Mind Mega Floette.

  • Quick Guard: Quick Guard is a niche move that can be used over Protect, Flare Blitz, or Will-O-Wisp. It protects allies against Fake Out users like Incineroar as well as other priority attacks like Aqua Jet from Basculegion-M and Sucker Punch from Kingambit.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Pokemon with Intimidate, such as Incineroar, severely weaken Talonflame's damage output. Rock Slide users like Garchomp, Tyranitar, and Aerodactyl are strong checks to Talonflame, as they are able to OHKO it. Garchomp is notable, as Rough Skin breaks Gale Wings regardless of what Flying-type move Talonflame is carrying. Furthermore, Mega Tyranitar's sand works similarly in breaking Gale Wings. Archaludon is also a great check to Talonflame, resisting its Flying-type moves and boosting up with Stamina. Fake Out users like Incineroar can break Talonflame's Gale Wings, removing the option to use priority Tailwind.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Garchomp and Mega Floette are some of the best Pokemon to pair Talonflame with. Talonflame's priority Tailwind and immunity to Earthquake allows Garchomp to put immense pressure on opponents. Additionally, Garchomp's Rock Slide in Tailwind lets it act as a great check against prominent Mega Charizard Y compositions by always outspeeding Mega Charizard Y in Tailwind. Mega Floette and Mega Gardevoir also benefit greatly from Tailwind, and Talonflame's STAB moves cover Sneasler and Kingambit for both. In return, their STAB Fairy-type moves handle Dragon-types like Garchomp and Dragonite. Kingambit discourages Pokemon with Intimidate from switching in with Defiant and provides high priority damage with Sucker Punch, which can OHKO opposing Basculegion-M. Finally, Choice Scarf Basculegion-M can take advantage of Tailwind by capitalizing on its powerful STAB attacks to KO threats such as Mega Aerodactyl. Additionally, bulky variants with Sitrus Berry or Mystic Water can use Tailwind to outspeed Mega Charizard Y, Mega Froslass, and Mega Gengar.

  • How to Overcome Talonflame's Weaknesses: Protecting Talonflame and preserving Gale Wings is a viable strategy against other Tailwind setters such as Aerodactyl and Whimsicott. Another viable strategy is to preserve Gale Wings for late-game scenarios, mainly by manually switching out. Kingambit can be used to threaten Basculegion-M and Mega Aerodactyl, which would otherwise use Aqua Jet or Rock Slide on Talonflame. Mega Floette also helps Talonflame, as its Light Of Ruin can quickly KO Archaludon and Garchomp.

Redirection Support.description:
• Vivillon is a fast supporter that gives offensive teams both disruption and redirection, forcing opponents to respect Compound Eyes-boosted Sleep Powder while using Rage Powder to protect teammates trying to set up or attack. These give it a niche different from bulkier redirection users such as Sinistcha and Maushold. Vivillon is useful next to teammates such as Mega Blastoise, Farigiraf, Kingambit, and Basculegion-M, which appreciate Vivillon creating openings without giving up too much offensive momentum.

  • Sleep Powder: Sleep Powder is Vivillon's main disruption tool, preventing a foe from acting and giving its partner room to set up or attack the other foe. Compound Eyes makes it reliable enough to threaten metagame staples such as Incineroar, Farigiraf, Kingambit, and Mega Charizard Y.

  • Hurricane: Hurricane prevents Vivillon from being completely passive after using its support moves, pressuring targets such as Sneasler, Kommo-o, Mega Venusaur, and Sinistcha. Even without Special Attack investment, Hurricane has a chance to OHKO Sneasler and always 2HKOes Kommo-o and Mega Venusaur. Hurricane also gives Vivillon something meaningful to do when Sleep Powder is blocked by Grass-types.

  • Pollen Puff versus Rain Dance versus Protect: Pollen Puff gives Vivillon a way to heal partners such as Mega Blastoise, Kingambit, and Basculegion-M after redirecting or forcing a sleep turn. Rain Dance is mainly for teams with Mega Blastoise or Basculegion-M, strengthening their Water-type attacks while removing sun from Mega Charizard Y and Torkoal. Protect should only be used on Focus Sash sets, as this lets Vivillon avoid Fake Out, stall opposing Pokemon's speed control, or preserve itself to use its powder moves later.

Items

  • Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf is preferred to make Vivillon a fast disruptor, letting it outspeed threats such as Mega Gengar, Mega Aerodactyl, Sneasler, Mega Froslass, and Choice Scarf Basculegion-M before putting them to sleep with Sleep Powder. However, being locked into Rage Powder or Sleep Powder can make Vivillon exploitable, especially if the opponent has Grass-types, which are immune to both moves, or spread attackers that can ignore Rage Powder.

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash trades Choice Scarf's Speed for more flexible move use, letting Vivillon switch between support and offense more freely. It is especially useful if Vivillon needs to survive a strong attack and still redirect an attack or put a foe to sleep, but it leaves Vivillon vulnerable to faster threats such as Mega Gengar, Mega Aerodactyl, and other Choice Scarf users.

Abilities

  • Compound Eyes: Compound Eyes makes Sleep Powder and Hurricane accurate enough for Vivillon to reliably disrupt and threaten Pokemon such as Sneasler, Incineroar, Farigiraf, Kingambit, and Mega Charizard Y. It also makes Hurricane much safer to use, letting Vivillon consistently punish targets like Sneasler, Kommo-o, Sinistcha, and Whimsicott instead of being limited to support moves. Compound Eyes is especially important on Choice Scarf sets, where missing Sleep Powder can make Vivillon's team lose a lot of momentum by giving the target a free turn to attack, set speed control, or reposition.

  • Friend Guard: Friend Guard can be used on Focus Sash sets if Vivillon's teammates value extra damage reduction, especially against spread moves that Rage Powder cannot redirect. However, losing Compound Eyes makes Sleep Powder and Hurricane much less reliable, so Friend Guard is usually worse.

SP Spreads

  • 24 Def / 5 SpA / 5 SpD / 32 Spe with Timid: This bulkier spread is mainly for Choice Scarf Vivillon. It keeps maximum Speed investment to outspeed key fast threats such as Mega Gengar, Mega Aerodactyl, Mega Froslass, and Choice Scarf Basculegion-M, as well as getting the jump on Adamant Choice Scarf Garchomp. The defensive investment lets Vivillon survive Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave and Sylveon's Hyper Voice, and it gives Vivillon an extremely good chance to survive Jolly Talonflame's Dual Wingbeat. Focus Sash sets can also consider this spread if they want to avoid being KOed by Talonflame's Dual Wingbeat.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Vivillon relies heavily on Sleep Powder to force progress, so Pokemon that can ignore Sleep Powder are its biggest obstacles. Sinistcha and Whimsicott are immune to Sleep Powder entirely. Whimsicott can use Prankster Encore to lock non-Choice Scarf Vivillon into Rage Powder, Sleep Powder, or Protect, while Sinistcha can set or remove Trick Room to disrupt Vivillon's team. Fake Out from Pokemon such as Sneasler, Incineroar, and Mega Kangaskhan can stop Vivillon before it uses its powder moves, which is especially punishing for Choice Scarf sets because they can't use Protect. Tailwind robs Vivillon much of its Speed advantage and makes it easier to KO. Gale Wings Talonflame is particularly threatening, as it can set priority-boosted Tailwind and can also threaten Vivillon directly with Flying-type STAB moves. Vivillon is also weak against strong spread damage moves, as Rage Powder cannot redirect moves like Garchomp's and Aerodactyl's Rock Slide, Mega Charizard Y's Heat Wave, Sylveon's Hyper Voice, and Mega Froslass's Blizzard. Rock-types can be major problems for Vivillon because they resist Hurricane, while Rock Slide hits it extremely effectively, bypasses Rage Powder, and pressures its partner all at the same time. Aerodactyl outspeeds non-Choice Scarf Vivillon and can KO Vivillon through Focus Sash or set Tailwind, and Mega Tyranitar can nullify Vivillon's Focus Sash with sand chip damage. Sun from Mega Charizard Y and Torkoal makes Hurricane much less reliable, limiting Vivillon's ability to deal respectable damage.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Vivillon should be paired with teammates that can immediately take advantage of the free turns it creates with its powder moves. Farigiraf is one of Vivillon's best partners, as Armor Tail blocks Fake Out, which would otherwise stop Vivillon from using Sleep Powder. In return, Vivillon can help Farigiraf set Trick Room through Rage Powder or by putting a foe to sleep. Mega Blastoise is one of Vivillon's strongest partners, as Vivillon's powder moves can create opportunities for it to use Shell Smash, while Pollen Puff can restore its HP to keep Water Spout strong. Rain Dance also strengthens Water Spout and removes sun from Mega Charizard Y and Torkoal. Basculegion-M similarly appreciates Rain Dance support, while Rage Powder can redirect Kingambit's Sucker Punch and give it safer turns to use Wave Crash or Last Respects. Sneasler threatens Rock- and Steel-types such as Mega Tyranitar, Kingambit, and Archaludon, which Vivillon struggles to damage. Incineroar can weaken physical attackers with Intimidate, which is especially useful for Choice Scarf Vivillon because Intimidate allows it to sometimes survive attacks it normally could not, such as Aerodactyl's Dual Wingbeat and Basculegion-M's Wave Crash. Additionally, Incineroar's Parting Shot can bring Vivillon or one of its offensive partners onto the field more safely. Kingambit appreciates Vivillon pressuring Fighting-types such as Sneasler and Kommo-o with Hurricane, while Vivillon can redirect Fighting-type attacks that threaten Kingambit. Mega Floette and Sylveon can pressure some Rock Slide users such as Mega Tyranitar and Garchomp with Fairy-type spread damage, while Vivillon helps them by threatening Sneasler with Hurricane and disrupting faster threats with Sleep Powder.

  • How to Overcome Vivillon's Weaknesses: Vivillon should avoid trying to use its powder moves against teams that can easily counter it. If Grass-types such as Sinistcha or Whimsicott are on the field, Hurricane is usually the better option, while Rage Powder should be saved for turns where it enables Vivillon's partner to attack or set up safely. Armor Tail from Farigiraf blocks Fake Out, Whimsicott's Prankster Encore, and Talonflame's Gale Wings Flying-type attacks while also letting Farigiraf set Trick Room in front of Tailwind teams. Incineroar can help Vivillon by using Fake Out to stop one foe while Vivillon puts the other to sleep. Because Rage Powder cannot redirect spread damage, Vivillon needs partners that can pressure common spread attackers directly. Mega Blastoise and Basculegion-M threaten Rock Slide and Heat Wave users such as Aerodactyl, Mega Charizard Y, and Torkoal, while Kingambit pressures Mega Froslass, Sylveon, and Mega Floette. Teammates such as Mega Blastoise, Basculegion-M, and Kingambit can pressure Rock-types like Mega Aerodactyl and Tyranitar, limiting their opportunities to force Vivillon out.

Sun Attacker.description:
• Mega Pyroar is a devastating sun attacker in Regulation M-B, taking advantage of Fire Mane and the sun to deal monstrous amounts of damage. Mega Pyroar's typing makes it immune to Basculegion-M's Last Respects and resistant to Gholdengo's and Mega Charizard Y's main STAB attacks as well as Fairy-type attacks from Mega Floette, Mega Gardevoir, and Sylveon.

  • Overheat: Overheat allows Mega Pyroar to OHKO nearly everything in the metagame with enough damage multipliers, including Pokemon that may resist Overheat, such as Incineroar and Garchomp.

  • Solar Beam: Solar Beam is used to hit Water-types like Basculegion-M, Mega Blastoise, and Mega Swampert for super effective damage.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Pelipper and Politoed can decrease Mega Pyroar's damage output with Drizzle while threatening it with rain-boosted Weather Ball. Rain allows Mega Swampert to outspeed and threaten Mega Pyroar with either STAB attack while denying Solar Beam as a coverage option.

  • Focus Sash Sneasler can survive one attack from Mega Pyroar and OHKO it back with Close Combat. Unburden-boosted Sneasler can also outspeed and OHKO Mega Pyroar. Sneasler's Fake Out can also slow down Mega Pyroar's momentum.

  • Garchomp and Basculegion-M resist Mega Pyroar's Fire-type moves while threatening to OHKO it with Life Orb-boosted Earthquake and Adaptability-boosted Wave Crash, respectively.
