  • Checks and Weaknesses: Despite Colbur Berry, Incineroar, Hydreigon, and Mega Tyranitar are still issues for Ceruledge, resisting both of Ceruledge's attacking moves and retaliating with Throat Chop, Dark Pulse, and Knock Off, respectively. Garchomp also heavily threatens Ceruledge with Earthquake and Stomping Tantrum while shrugging off Bitter Blade and Shadow Sneak. Basculegion-M can easily OHKO Ceruledge with 100 Base Power Last Respects and Wave Crash, the latter of which even OHKOes Ceruledge after it uses Bulk Up. Mega Blastoise and Milotic also threaten huge Water-type damage with Water Spout and Muddy Water, respectively; Milotic can even use Coil to match Ceruledge's Bulk Up boosts. Rock-type Pokemon like Hisuian Arcanine, Mega Aerodactyl, and the aforementioned Mega Tyranitar all resist Bitter Blade and threaten Ceruledge with Rock Slide.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Floette hits the Dark- and Dragon-types that Ceruledge struggles with, while Ceruledge provides help against Mega Charizard Y and Steel-types like Corviknight in return. Milotic and Sneasler provide coverage against Dark- and Rock-type Pokemon, both notably scaring away Incineroar with Competitive and White Herb, respectively. Sinistcha is able to redirect Water-type attacks with ease and hit Water-types with Matcha Gotcha. It often carries Kasib Berry to even redirect Ghost-type attacks like Shadow Ball from Mega Froslass, giving Ceruledge space to set up.

  • How to Overcome Ceruledge's Weaknesses: Ceruledge must be paired with offensive threats that can handle the foes it can't, such as Mega Floette, which often fulfills this role. It forms a strong offensive duo with Ceruledge, handling the Dragon-types that resist Ceruledge's Bitter Blade, while Ceruledge hits the Steel-types that resist Mega Floette's Fairy-type attacks. On the defensive side, Fake Out and redirection support from Incineroar and Sinistcha give Ceruledge a far easier time setting up. To keep Ceruledge strong, answers to Intimidate users, particularly Incineroar, are important. Milotic and Sneasler threaten Incineroar with big damage, while Kingambit can also deter it, though not as effectively, as Kingambit itself fears Flare Blitz.

Redirection Support.description:
• Mega Scovillain uses Spicy Spray and Rage Powder to punish physical attackers like Basculegion-M, Garchomp, and Kingambit while keeping its teammates safe. It also threatens high burst damage with Overheat against foes like Whimsicott and Sinistcha. Between burn's Attack drop, recovery from Leech Seed or Giga Drain, and even a lucky defensive boost from Moody before Mega Evolving, Mega Scovillain can make itself incredibly difficult to remove from the field.

  • Rage Powder and Spicy Spray: Rage Powder can force foes to attack Mega Scovillain and activate Spicy Spray, mitigating damage from physical attackers to keep its allies safe. Mega Scovillain is typically meant to be led to apply burn pressure early-game, which can also dissuade physical attackers from attacking, giving an ally like Kingambit room to set up Swords Dance to help it take out threats. Leading Mega Scovillain can pressure Basculegion-M to switch out, at which point saving Mega Scovillain for later may be necessary to burn it and stop it from sweeping with Last Respects.

  • Giga Drain versus Leech Seed: Giga Drain threatens good damage against Basculegion-M and Mega Blastoise while providing instantaneous healing. Leech Seed can rack up considerable passive damage, especially when combined with a burn. Leech Seed also allows Mega Scovillain to effectively ignore its Special Attack drop from Overheat by pivoting to a passive playstyle.

  • Mega Evolving Scovillain: Protect can be used before Mega Evolving to fish for useful Moody boosts. A Speed boost will allow Mega Scovillain to outrun Sneasler, a Defense boost will allow it to survive 200-Base Power Last Respects from Basculegion-M, and a Special Defense boost will allow it to survive Sludge Bomb from Mega Gengar. Delaying Mega Evolution can also prompt an opponent to consider whether a different Pokemon will Mega Evolve later.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 10 Def / 24 SpD with Bold: The defensive investment allows Mega Scovillain to always survive Dire Claw from Sneasler and avoid a 2HKO from Garchomp's Dragon Claw. The remaining SPs are put into Special Defense to survive Weather Ball from bulky Mega Charizard Y and Hurricane from Vivillon.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Fire-types are unaffected by Spicy Spray, and Mega Charizard Y in particular threatens to deal heavy damage to Mega Scovillain. Incineroar can safely use Fake Out on Mega Scovillain, shutting down Rage Powder support for a turn, shrug off Overheat, and pivot out of Leech Seed easily with Parting Shot. Rain teams typically feature Pelipper, which threatens Mega Scovillain with Hurricane and weakens its Overheat with Drizzle. Mega Gengar threatens an OHKO with Sludge Bomb, counters Mega Scovillain's slower playstyle with a Perish trap strategy, and can use Disable on Rage Powder to stop Mega Gengar's teammates from getting burned. Most special attackers in general are comfortable against Mega Scovillain because they do not care about being burned.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Teammates like Basculegion-M and Kingambit appreciate Mega Scovillain's ability to redirect strong attacks like Sucker Punch and Close Combat, respectively, weakening the users in case they get another chance to attack later in the game. These are also offensive Pokemon that can make up for Mega Scovillain's lower damage output. Mega Froslass offers a more offensive playstyle, works better against Perish trap because it can freely switch out of Shadow Tag, and is a better option than Mega Scovillain against opposing rain. Mega Aerodactyl can be brought instead of Mega Scovillain against its biggest threats such as Mega Charizard Y and Sneasler, or Lycanroc-D can cover Mega Charizard Y without using Mega Evolution. Archaludon appreciates Sneasler's Close Combat being weakened by burn and improves the matchup against rain.

  • How to Overcome Mega Scovillain's Weaknesses: Rock-type coverage from teammates like Lycanroc-D and Mega Aerodactyl is mandatory for dealing with Mega Charizard Y. Steel-type coverage from Kingambit or Archaludon is appreciated to cover Rock-type foes like Aerodactyl or Glimmora that threaten Mega Scovillain, and both of them help the matchup against Incineroar. Archaludon covers Flying-type threats like Pelipper and Mega Charizard Y with Electro Shot.

Offensive.description:
• With its typing, Glimmora can resist the STAB moves of multiple attackers in the format, making it a good check to Mega Charizard Y, Mega Floette, and Aerodactyl. Furthermore, its own STAB moves can OHKO several common threats, such as Mega Charizard Y, Aerodactyl, and Whimsicott, while pressuring most of the metagame for super effective damage.

  • Earth Power is used to threaten Steel-types such as Archaludon and Kingambit that both resist its STAB moves and are immune to Toxic Spikes.

Ability

  • Toxic Debris punishes physical attackers that attack Glimmora. With Focus Sash, Toxic Spikes can be set up more reliably. This helps punish Pokemon that like to pivot in and out often, such as Incineroar.

Items

  • Focus Sash protects Glimmora from being OHKOed by some of the format's heavier hitters, such as Garchomp, Basculegion-M, and Mega Delphox. Focus Sash further helps Glimmora by granting it more opportunities to set up Toxic Spikes through its ability.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Metagame staples such as Garchomp and Mega Delphox reliably outspeed Glimmora, threatening major damage. Furthermore, even though it can hit many Pokemon for super effective damage, Glimmora can still fail to OHKO them. For example, Mega Floette requires two Sludge Bombs to be taken out. Similarly, Kingambit can tank an Earth Power and OHKO back with Iron Head. Special attackers like Mega Delphox and Rotom-Wash threaten to OHKO Glimmora without triggering Toxic Debris.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Whimsicott is a strong ally for Glimmora, using its Prankster-boosted Tailwind to reliably set the pace of the battle for Glimmora to outspeed threats such as Mega Floette while using STAB Fairy-type attacks to check Garchomp. Additionally, Glimmora can help OHKO Sneasler, which Whimsicott can struggle with. Mega Charizard Y is another good partner; its Fire-type STAB moves help check Steel-types, and its Drought protects Glimmora from Water-type attacks such as Wave Crash from Basculegion-M. Mega Charizard Y likewise benefits from Glimmora, as Glimmora's Power Gem can hit Incineroar , which would otherwise resist Mega Charizard Y’s attacks, for super effective damage.

  • How To Overcome Glimmora's Weaknesses: Partnering Glimmora with Mega Charizard Y helps it cover threats such as Basculegion-M and Rotom-Wash with Solar Beam, and the sun weakens their Water-type attacks. Additionally, Kingambit threatens Farigiraf and Mega Delphox, which can threaten Glimmora with Twin Beam and Psyshock, respectively.

Glass Cannon.description:
• Annihilape uses its excellent offensive coverage, solid Speed, and immunity to common defensive tools like Intimidate and Fake Out to dismantle opposing teams and create awkward situations for the opponent with Phantom Force. It also has incredible matchups against metagame staples like Incineroar, Sneasler, and Kingambit.

  • Phantom Force: Phantom Force forces common setup Pokemon like Mega Delphox, Gholdengo, and Mega Gengar to either switch out or take devastating damage. Phantom Force also breaks Protect, which can allow a slower partner to attack Annihilape's target even if they use Protect.

  • Rock Tomb vs. Rage Fist: Rock Tomb can be used for speed control and allows Annihilape to deal big damage to Mega Charizard Y. Rage Fist can be used as an alternate Ghost-type attack. Its damage output is slightly higher than Phantom Force after Annihilape gets hit once, and at 150 Base Power, Rage Fist can OHKO Sinistcha, Gholdengo, and Sneasler.

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash is needed to let Annihilape check Pokemon like Mega Delphox and Mega Gengar that could otherwise outspeed and OHKO it with moves like Psychic and Shadow Ball respectively.

  • Defiant: Defiant makes Annihilape great at deterring Intimidate users. When combined with Annihilape's Fake Out immunity and Close Combat, it makes Annihilape a perfect counter to Incineroar.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Fast Fairy-types like Mega Floette, Whimsicott, and Sylveon under Tailwind can 2HKO Annihilape while tanking a Phantom Force or Rage Fist. Mega Staraptor can similarly outspeed and threaten Annihilape with Brave Bird while also being able to tank any of its attacks; however, it can take big damage from Phantom Force or a boosted Rage Fist combined with Brave Bird's recoil. Mega Aerodactyl can outspeed and OHKO Annihilape through its Focus Sash with Dual Wingbeat.

  • Redirection: Maushold and Mega Scovillain are particularly bad redirectors for Annihilape to deal with. Maushold can nullify Phantom Force's damage due to its Ghost immunity, while Mega Scovillain can burn Annihilape thanks to Spicy Spray, which not only reduces Annihilape's offensive prowess but also breaks its Focus Sash.

  • Farigiraf: Farigiraf can safely switch into Phantom Force while also being able to tank a Close Combat. Farigiraf can also remove Annihilape's Speed advantage with Trick Room and 2HKO it with Psychic.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Mega Charizard Y is one of Annihilape's best partners due to its Fairy resistance and ability to deal big damage to Annihilape's checks. Mega Charizard Y's sun-boosted Heat Wave ignores redirection and can 2HKO Maushold and Mega Scovillain, while Weather Ball can 2HKO Farigiraf through its Sitrus Berry healing. In return, Annihilape can force out Basculegion-M and Incineroar, which are common checks to Mega Charizard Y.

  • Poison-types: With Chlorophyll, Venusaur in the sun can outspeed and threaten Fairy-types with Sludge Bomb. If given a Life Orb, it can outspeed and OHKO Mega Aerodactyl with Solar Beam. Toxapex can sit in front of Fairy-types and take them down over time with the combination of Toxic and Infestation. Toxapex can also trap Pokemon on the field with Infestation, forcing them to get hit by Phantom Force. Phantom Force combined with Protect can let Annihilape stall out turns, letting Toxapex's Infestation and Toxic rack up damage before Phantom Force KOes the target.

  • Incineroar and Garchomp: Incineroar can use Fake Out to let Annihilape set up a Phantom Force and can threaten Farigiraf with Throat Chop. Intimidate also drops Mega Aerodactyl's Attack low enough so that it can't OHKO Annihilape with Dual Wingbeat. Incineroar appreciates Annihilape's good matchups against Sneasler and Basculegion-M. Choice Scarf Garchomp can outspeed and deal big damage to Mega Aerodactyl with Rock Slide, and it appreciates Annihilape's ability to threaten Hydreigon.

Trick Room Support.description:
• Farigiraf's solid resilience and unique ability to deny Fake Out give it a strong niche as a reliable Trick Room setter. Offensively, a Psychic typing grants it a great matchup against Poison-types like Sneasler, Glimmora, and Venusaur.

  • Psychic: Even with no Special Attack investment, Psychic will always 2HKO maximum HP variants of Mega Gengar and Mega Venusaur.

  • Thunderbolt vs. Hyper Voice: Thunderbolt pressures Flying- and Water-types like Mega Charizard Y, Mega Aerodactyl, and Basculegion-M, notably having a good chance to 2HKO the latter two with no investment. Hyper Voice sacrifices useful coverage for the ability to constantly pressure the opposing team with spread damage, especially if Farigiraf has the initiative under Trick Room.

  • Protect vs. Helping Hand: If Farigiraf's support is integral to your team, it can use Protect to defensively position itself and guard against double targeting. Helping Hand can be used over Protect if you can afford to sacrifice Farigiraf, allowing it to bolster the team's damage output even when it's about to be KOed. Farigiraf can run both moves in the last two moveslots only if it's supporting a Pokemon that can deal so much spread damage, like Torkoal or Mega Blastoise, that having an auxiliary attack isn't necessary.

Other Options

  • Twin Beam: Twin Beam is a weaker alternative to Psychic that's capable of OHKOing Focus Sash variants of Sneasler and, with enough investment, Glimmora.

  • Roar: Roar can be used in the last moveslot to deny setup sweepers like Mega Floette from gaining boosts and users of Trick Room like Sinistcha and opposing Farigiraf from setting it up.

  • Ally Switch: Although it's reliant on predicting your opponent's actions, Ally Switch's ability to essentially redirect an incoming attack away from Farigiraf's ally can make it a worthwhile consideration for the last moveslot.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry's burst healing lets Farigiraf repeatedly survive strong attacks like Sneasler's Close Combat and handle double targeting much more easily, making it the preferred held item.

  • Colbur Berry: If Sitrus Berry isn't available, Colbur Berry can be used to guarantee survival against Black Glasses Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave and Mega Tyranitar's Knock Off.

Abilities

  • Armor Tail: Armor Tail's most notable application is denying Fake Out from users like Sneasler and Incineroar. Additionally, it protects Farigiraf's team from Kingambit's Sucker Punch and Prankster-boosted moves like Whimsicott's Encore and Sableye's Quash.

SP Spreads

  • Speed-reducing Natures: A Relaxed, Quiet, or Sassy nature can be used over a Bold, Modest, or Calm nature, respectively, if you want Farigiraf to outspeed neutral-natured base 60s like Sylveon and Incineroar under Trick Room.

  • 30 HP / 24 Def / 12 SpD with Bold or Relaxed: This is a physically defensive spread that lets Farigiraf survive Black Glasses Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave and Mega Scizor's Bug Bite. With Sitrus Berry, Farigiraf is also likely to avoid getting 2HKOed by Sneasler's Close Combat, Jolly Adaptability Basculegion-M's Wave Crash, and Modest Mega Floette's Dazzling Gleam.

  • 12 HP / 24 Def / 27 SpA / 3 SpD with Modest or Quiet: This offensive spread lets Farigiraf usually OHKO Focus Sash Glimmora with Twin Beam and potentially OHKO maximum HP Mega Gengar with Psychic. The bulk investment lets Farigiraf avoid the OHKO from non-Black Glasses Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave and Mega Floette's Moonblast, as well as the 2HKO from uninvested Incineroar's Throat Chop with either Berry.

  • 32 HP / 11 Def / 23 SpD with Calm or Sassy: With the heavy special bulk investment, Farigiraf cannot be OHKOed by Mega Floette's Light of Ruin and is unlikely to be OHKOed by its +1 Moonblast, while 11 Defense SPs give favorable odds to survive non-Black Glasses Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave. Sitrus Berry lets Farigiraf dodge the 2HKO from Mega Charizard Y's Heat Wave and Archaludon's Electro Shot, as well as the 3HKO from Jolly Garchomp's Dragon Claw almost all of the time.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Kingambit is the most threatening Pokemon to Farigiraf, as it can easily KO non-Colbur Berry variants with Kowtow Cleave, comfortably take Farigiraf's STAB attacks, and benefit from Trick Room with its low Speed. Additionally, Farigiraf is a sitting duck against other Dark-types like Mega Tyranitar and Incineroar; Mega Tyranitar can threaten an OHKO with Knock Off and proceed to set up as it switches out, while Incineroar can gradually wear it down and lock out Hyper Voice with Throat Chop. Steel-types like Aegislash and Corviknight easily tank Farigiraf's STAB attacks, which lets them freely attack and, in Corviknight's case, set up. Bug-types like Kleavor and Mega Scizor pressure Farigiraf with their STAB moves; additionally, Mega Scizor can set up Swords Dance and gain free recovery by eating its Sitrus Berry with Bug Bite. Although it's fairly bulky, Farigiraf can be easily KOed if it's targeted by a pair of very strong foes; a combination of attacks like Mega Charizard Y's Weather Ball and Sneasler's Close Combat can put it out of commission if it attempts to set up Trick Room. Farigiraf's lack of coverage and Speed can make it passive outside of Trick Room, especially if it uses a bulky SP spread. This can put the burden on its on-field ally to pick up the slack offensively, which the opponent can exploit by double targeting the ally.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Farigiraf should be ideally paired with slow teammates like Kingambit and Sylveon, as they appreciate the ability to attack first and still tank a couple blows with their bulk investment. However, it's possible to use Farigiraf alongside moderately fast Pokemon like Mega Charizard Y and Mega Floette, especially if the opposing team uses Tailwind support. In this case, a Tailwind setter like Whimsicott or Aerodactyl can be beneficial for an alternate team mode if Trick Room isn't needed, and Farigiraf can still contribute to this mode by blocking Fake Out with Armor Tail to preserve the setter's Focus Sash. This also prevents Pokemon that don't run Protect, like Choice Scarf Garchomp and most Chople Berry Kingambit variants, from getting disrupted and losing momentum.

  • Kingambit appreciates Farigiraf's ability to pressure Sneasler; in return, it can handle Aegislash and, with Low Kick, other Dark-types like opposing Kingambit and Mega Tyranitar. Fairy-types like Sylveon and Mega Floette can repay Farigiraf's good matchup against Poison-types by handling Dark-types for it; Sylveon can use Trick Room to attack unimpeded, while bulky Calm Mind variants of Mega Floette can have an easier time setting up under it. Fire-types like Torkoal and Mega Charizard Y can blast through Steel- and Bug-types with their STAB moves. Torkoal especially stands out given its absolutely subpar Speed, which, in tandem with Armor Tail, makes it almost guaranteed to unleash a full-power Eruption under Trick Room. Incineroar can also handle these foes itself under Trick Room, and it can help protect Farigiraf from getting overwhelmed with Fake Out, Intimidate, and Parting Shot.

  • How to Overcome Farigiraf's Weaknesses: Farigiraf should be positioned in a way such that it won't be KOed if it attempts to set up Trick Room. When paired with it as the leading duo, Incineroar can prevent double targeting with Fake Out, letting Farigiraf set up Trick Room more easily. Once Trick Room is set up, Incineroar can pivot to an offensive teammate to maintain momentum. Under Trick Room, Farigiraf should ideally be paired with the teammate that threatens the opposing side the best or switch out if two offensive Pokemon can put up better pressure. Outside of Trick Room, it can get around its Speed with Helping Hand to still contribute to the team's damage output. If your team has a Tailwind setter alongside Farigiraf, determine the opposing team's means of speed control and potential priority users during Team Preview, then play off your selections from there. For example, if the opposing team has its own Tailwind setter and a Fake Out user, it may be wise to bench your setter and bring Farigiraf instead.

Bulky Attacker.description:
• Kingambit is one of the top threats of Regulation M-B, trading damage comfortably and threatening many top threats such as Basculegion-M, Gholdengo, and Mega Floette. Additionally, Kingambit's typing allows it to defensively answer both Gholdengo's and Mega Metagross's STAB moves as well as making it immune to Toxapex's Toxic.

  • Items: Black Glasses allows Kingambit to deal more damage with Kowtow Cleave and Sucker Punch. Black Glasses-boosted Sucker Punch always OHKOes Choice Scarf Basculegion-M and can OHKO Mega Froslass in the snow most of the time. Focus Sash allows Kingambit to sacrifice its defenses to patch up its lackluster Speed, and it enables Kingambit to survive strong attacks such as Mega Floette's Light of Ruin, Mega Staraptor's Close Combat, and Mega Charizard Y's Weather Ball. Focus Sash Kingambit is utilized on Tailwind teams to take advantage of any Speed investment. Chople Berry lets Kingambit retain its great bulk and utilize Trick Room better while surviving Jolly Sneasler's Close Combat, Low Kick from opposing Kingambit and Tyranitar, and Mega Raichu Y's Focus Blast. Chople Berry Kingambit can also survive Mega Staraptor's Close Combat, but this isn't guaranteed.

  • Abilities: Defiant allows Kingambit to punish Incineroar's and Staraptor's Intimidate, Milotic's Icy Wind, and even the Special Attack drops from Mega Floette's and Whimsicott's Moonblast. Defiant's boost lets Kingambit always OHKO Sinistcha with Kowtow Cleave.

  • Sucker Punch: Sucker Punch makes up for Kingambit's poor Speed and threatens faster Pokemon such as Basculegion-M. Sucker Punch is also useful for late-game one-on-ones, as it pressures the opponent to guess whether Kingambit will choose Kowtow Cleave or Sucker Punch.

  • Iron Head versus Swords Dance versus Low Kick: Iron Head is used to threaten Mega Floette and Sylveon while dealing decent damage to Sneasler and Mega Staraptor and chunking Tyranitar. Swords Dance turns Kingambit into a setup sweeper; it's typically seen with Black Glasses to add another damage multiplier. A Black Glasses- and Swords Dance-boosted Sucker Punch can OHKO frailer Mega Charizard Y and Garchomp. Low Kick is used to threaten opposing Kingambit, Incineroar, and Tyranitar. However, Kingambit cannot damage Fairy-types or Sneasler much if it opts for Low Kick.

  • Protect versus Low Kick: Low Kick is an alternative coverage move if Kingambit doesn't necessarily need Protect on its team. This comes at the cost of Kingambit being unable to shield itself from Fake Out and attacks that may threaten it. Focus Sash and Chople Berry are typically seen with this option, because it allows Kingambit to trade damage more comfortably.

Other Options

  • Life Orb: Life Orb pushes Kingambit's power to the absolute limit, at the cost of some recoil. A Life Orb-boosted Sucker Punch OHKOes some Gholdengo.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 32 Atk / 2 Def with Adamant: This is Kingambit's primary SP spread. Chople Berry and Black Glasses are typically seen with this spread.

  • 2 HP / 32 Atk / 32 Spe with Adamant: This spread is used with a set utilizing four attacks and Focus Sash, allowing Kingambit to outspeed bulkier Pelipper and some Incineroar.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Even with Chople Berry, Kingambit does not have the best matchup against Sneasler and Mega Staraptor. Low Kick from opposing Kingambit and Tyranitar threaten to OHKO Kingambit as well, and without speed control, Tyranitar will beat Black Glasses Kingambit. Despite Kingambit's ability acting as a check to Incineroar's Intimidate, its Flare Blitz still threatens Kingambit.

  • Without Iron Head or a Swords Dance boost, Mega Floette and Sylveon will outlast Kingambit in damage trades. Additionally, Mega Floette's Light of Ruin will OHKO non-Focus Sash Kingambit.

  • Mega Charizard Y is faster than Kingambit and will threaten to OHKO it, while Excadrill, Mega Swampert, and Garchomp are Ground-types that threaten Kingambit super effectively while also outspeeding it.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Basculegion-M and Sinistcha can block Sneasler's Close Combat, and the former can OHKO Sneasler with Wave Crash while resisting Dire Claw. Furthermore, Basculegion-M also threatens Incineroar for huge damage even with Intimidate. Sinistcha can set up Trick Room for Kingambit, allowing Kingambit to outspeed and beat threats to Sinistcha, such as non-Focus Sash Basculegion and Mega Froslass.

  • Sneasler can threaten opposing Kingambit and Mega Tyranitar with Close Combat and provide Fake Out support so that Kingambit can set up a Swords Dance safely. Kingambit can deal with Gholdengo and Mega Metagross in return.

  • Mega Charizard Y can support Kingambit teams with its immunity to Garchomp's Earthquake and resistance to Incineroar's Flare Blitz, opposing Mega Charizard Y's Heat Wave and sun-boosted Weather Ball, and Mega Staraptor's Close Combat while pressuring opposing Kingambit and Mega Scovillain. In return, Kingambit can cover Mega Aerodactyl for it.

  • Garchomp can threaten opposing Kingambit, Mega Charizard Y, Sneasler, and Tyranitar. Kingambit boasts an excellent matchup against Mega Froslass, as well as Alolan Ninetales if it is running Iron Head, both of which Garchomp usually struggles with. However, Garchomp cannot safely use Earthquake next to Kingambit.

  • Mega Floette and Sylveon can threaten opposing Garchomp, Hydreigon, and Mega Staraptor. Their weakness to Poison-type moves such as Sneasler's Poison Jab and Venusaur's Sludge Bomb is in turn patched up by Kingambit's Steel typing.

Setup Sweeper.description:
• Gholdengo, thanks to its naturally strong defensive typing, easily walls out common Pokemon like Sneasler and Mega Staraptor and helps beat top Pokemon like Mega Floette, Sylveon, Mega Aerodactyl, and Sinistcha. This typing allows Gholdengo to set up Nasty Plot, letting it sweep through teams with its STAB moves and threaten nearly all metagame staples with at least neutral damage.

  • Make It Rain: Make It Rain hits nearly anything that doesn't resist it for huge damage after a Nasty Plot, having a solid chance to OHKO Mega Tyranitar with Life Orb. When using Make It Rain, Gholdengo must be careful; using it at the wrong time late-game will leave Gholdengo too weak to contribute much . This forces Gholdengo to use Nasty Plot again and leave itself or its partner open to attacks.

  • Life Orb: Life Orb gives Gholdengo potential for large amounts of burst damage, allowing Gholdengo to OHKO most Mega Froslass with Make It Rain and Basculegion-M with Shadow Ball, though it comes at the cost of Gholdengo's longevity. For this reason, builds that use Life Orb Gholdengo tend to run faster and more offensive SP spreads to turn it into a strong and threatening attacker that doesn't require setup turns.

  • Spell Tag and Metal Coat: Spell Tag and Metal Coat save Gholdengo's longevity but only allow it to boost either Shadow Ball or Make it Rain. Spell Tag allows Gholdengo to 2HKO Sneasler, while Metal Coat allows Gholdengo to OHKO Mega Aerodactyl.

  • Good as Gold: Good as Gold gives Gholdengo good chances to switch into attacks like Parting Shot from Incineroar and Grimmsnarl as well as Sleep Powder from Venusaur.

Other Options

  • Leftovers: Leftovers allow Gholdengo to focus more on setting up by increasing its longevity, though the item sacrifices power.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 8 Def / 7 SpA / 3 SpD / 16 Spe with Timid: The given SP spread allows Gholdengo to outspeed Adamant Basculegion-M, almost always survive Earthquake from Jolly Life Orb Garchomp, and withstand Dark Pulse from Mega Blastoise, with the rest dumped into Special Attack.

  • 7 HP / 32 SpA / 27 Spe with Timid: This SP spread is tailored towards Life Orb sets. It lets Gholdengo outrun Jolly Basculegion-M and survive Wave Crash from Choice Scarf Adamant Basculegion-M, allowing Gholdengo to retaliate with Shadow Ball. The remaining SPs are put into Special Attack.

  • 17 HP / 1 Def / 15 SpA / 1 SpD / 32 Spe with Modest: With the SPs in HP, Defense, and Special Defense, Gholdengo can possibly survive Flare Blitz from Incineroar and has a high chance to survive Heat Wave from Timid Mega Delphox. The SPs in Special Attack allow Life Orb-boosted Shadow Ball to OHKO Mega Delphox and +2 Make It Rain to OHKO uninvested Mega Tyranitar, which typically uses Dragon Dance sets. The Speed SPs allow Gholdengo to outspeed all Mega Tyranitar.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Fire-type Pokemon like Mega Charizard Y, Mega Blaziken, Incineroar, and Mega Scovillain threaten huge damage onto Gholdengo with Heat Wave, Weather Ball, Flare Blitz, and Overheat. Incineroar in particular resists both of Gholdengo's STAB options, tanking Make It Rain and Shadow Ball and retaliating with Throat Chop or Flare Blitz.

  • Ghost-types like Basculegion-M and Mega Gengar outspeed and threaten to OHKO Gholdengo with Last Respects and Shadow Ball. Hydreigon, Kingambit, and Mega Tyranitar are Dark-types that OHKO Gholdengo with Dark Pulse, Kowtow Cleave, and Knock Off. Additionally, Hydreigon can opt for Snarl instead to slowly chip down Gholdengo and weaken it in the process, and Kingambit can use Sucker Punch to hit Gholdengo before it moves.

  • Ground-types like Mega Swampert and Garchomp threaten Gholdengo with Earthquake. Mega Swampert also resists Make It Rain and is placed on rain teams alongside Pokemon like Hydreigon and Archaludon, which can deal lots of damage to Gholdengo with Dark Pulse and Electro Shot. On the other hand, Garchomp's flexibility enables it to fit on many teams, meaning that it is a hurdle that Gholdengo often has to face.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Garchomp threatens Fire-types aside from Mega Scovillain with Earthquake, and it can handle Mega Charizard Y with Rock Slide.

  • Incineroar and Kingambit can switch into Ghost-types and threaten them with Throat Chop and Kowtow Cleave, while Sneasler and Mega Staraptor can help Gholdengo handle Dark-types with Close Combat.

  • Sinistcha can heal up Gholdengo with Hospitality and redirect many attacks with Rage Powder; it can also switch into Ground-types and threaten Mega Swampert with Matcha Gotcha. Alolan Ninetales can threaten Ground-types with Freeze-Dry and Blizzard.

Redirection Support.description:
• Sinistcha is the go-to redirector in the Regulation M-A metagame, setting itself apart from other redirectors with its immunity to Fake Out, good defensive stats, access to Trick Room, and Hospitality. Its typing allows it to support metagame-defining threats well, redirecting away moves such as Sneasler's Close Combat and Dire Claw, as well as Water-type moves and Electro Shot from rain teams.

  • Trick Room versus Protect: Trick Room is useful to turn the tables on fast threats, like Chlorophyll Venusaur, and Tailwind, even when it necessarily isn't used for a Trick Room sweeper. However, Protect can be used over Trick Room if there is conflict with other speed control options on Sinistcha's team or to give Sinistcha another tool to assist with positioning itself or other teammates.

  • Life Dew versus Protect: Life Dew is great for partners with setup moves, particularly Calm Mind Mega Floette. When using Trick Room, Protect could be used over Life Dew to help position Sinistcha to safely set it up. For instance, Sinistcha can use Protect while its partner switches to a Fake Out user, which would then give it a better opportunity to set Trick Room.

Other Options

  • Strength Sap: Strength Sap is a rather effective self-healing option, in addition to being a way to manage physical threats such as Garchomp and Incineroar.

  • Shadow Ball: Shadow Ball is a more proactive tool to help manage the common Ghost-types in the metagame, such as other Sinistcha, Mega Gengar, Mega Froslass, and Ceruledge, as well as some Psychic-types like Mega Delphox.

Items

  • Kasib Berry: With Kasib Berry, Basculegion-M can't OHKO Sinistcha with a 150-Base Power Last Respects, while Sinistcha resists its Water-type STAB moves and threatens to both 2HKO Basculegion-M with Matcha Gotcha.

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry is useful for general healing and helps Sinistcha avoid 2HKOs from attacks such as Fairy Feather Sylveon's Hyper Voice, Mega Floette's Moonblast, Mega Aerodactyl's Dual Wingbeat after Intimidate, and Incineroar's Flare Blitz after Intimidate.

  • Colbur Berry: Colbur Berry is most useful to help manage Kingambit, allowing Sinistcha to take a Kowtow Cleave more easily; instead of requiring Sinistcha to stay at full HP to survive Kowtow Cleave, it only needs half of its HP. This allows Sinistcha to more safely use Rage Powder in front of Kingambit, nullifying Sucker Punch and allowing its partner to attack safely.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 14 Def / 20 SpD with Bold: The Defense investment allows Sinistcha to avoid being OHKOed by Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave. The rest of the SPs are invested into Special Defense for general bulk. A Relaxed nature could also be used for Trick Room, though it doesn't allow Sinistcha to underspeed anything noteworthy aside from other Sinistcha.

  • 32 HP / 11 Def / 23 SpD with Calm This spread allows Sinistcha to more effectively redirect special attacks, notably Timid Mega Gengar's Shadow Ball, with the remaining SPs invested into Defense. More Special Defense could be used to live attacks such as Timid Mega Floette's Light of Ruin, though it comes at the cost of taking more damage from common physical attackers like Kingambit and Incineroar.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Sinistcha has many exploitable weaknesses, most notably Mega Charizard Y's sun-boosted Heat Wave, which both ignores Rage Powder and OHKOes Sinistcha. Mega Froslass with Blizzard and Mega Delphox with Heat Wave are similarly effective against Rage Powder Sinistcha, (AC) even if they don't OHKO it. Mega Aerodactyl with Dual Wingbeat and Kingambit with Kowtow Cleave do significant damage to Sinistcha. Ceruledge can 2HKO Sinistcha with Bitter Blade or OHKO it after a Bulk Up while resisting Matcha Gotcha and being immune to burn. Basculegion-M, while being 2HKOed by Matcha Gotcha, can threaten an OHKO with a boosted Last Respects unless Sinistcha holds a Kasib Berry. Mega Tyranitar is similar; it can outright OHKO Sinistcha with Knock Off and is naturally faster than Sinistcha to avoid Matcha Gotcha. Incineroar both resists and cannot be burned by Matcha Gotcha, and it can chunk Sinistcha for around half its health with Throat Chop or for even more with Flare Blitz. Pelipper is often a rain team's first line of defense against Sinistcha, as its Hurricane OHKOes it after slight chip damage.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Hospitality makes Sinistcha a great partner for Mega Floette, which also appreciates redirection for threatening attacks like Sneasler's Dire Claw or Gunk Shot while it sets up. Mega Floette can then threaten to OHKO Sinistcha checks such as Kingambit with a +1 Moonblast or spread damage with Dazzling Gleam. Other Pokemon that use boosting moves can naturally make excellent use of Sinistcha's redirection and Hospitality. Black Glasses Swords Dance Kingambit and Dragon Dance Mega Tyranitar are a couple of Pokemon that appreciate being able to set up in the face of extremely effective Close Combats from Sneasler and can threaten Sinistcha's checks; they outspeed and OHKO Mega Charizard Y with Sucker Punch and Rock Slide, respectively, after a boost. Slower Pokemon such as Kingambit and non-Choice Scarf Basculegion-M can most effectively take advantage of Sinistcha's Trick Room.

  • Overcoming Sinistcha's Weaknesses: Incineroar can both make use of the extra healing and complements Sinistcha's typing near-perfectly, forming a core that can switch into each other's weaknesses and repeatedly activate Intimidate and Hospitality. Fake Out can help ensure Trick Room is set up, and Parting Shot can also allow Sinistcha to heal a teammate in the same turn by switching out Sinistcha, using Parting Shot, then switching it back in again mid-turn. While Incineroar does give Kingambit a Defiant boost, it still resists Kingambit's STAB moves and threatens to 2HKO with Flare Blitz. Similar to Incineroar, Basculegion-M both resists Fire and has access to Flip Turn to pivot. Choice Scarf Basculegion-M can also threaten key threats to Sinistcha such as Mega Aerodactyl and Mega Delphox with its speedy Wave Crash, and although Mega Charizard Y can mitigate the damage with Drought, it will still be easily 2HKOed with Wave Crash while Sinistcha threatens to redirect its Solar Beam. Sneasler threatens Kingambit and other Dark-types with STAB Close Combat. Kingambit itself is a good source of Fighting-type damage with Low Kick and a partner Sinistcha is a great way to avoid Low Kick from opposing Kingambit. Kingambit additionally helps overcome Ghost-type threats such as Mega Froslass and Basculegion-M. Garchomp is an excellent check to both Mega Charizard Y and Kingambit, 2HKOing both with Rock Slide and Earthquake, respectively; Mega Charizard Y is even able to be OHKOed if it does not have Defense investment. Pelipper and Politoed effectively neuter Sinistcha's biggest check in Mega Charizard Y, as well as other Fire-types such as Incineroar and Mega Delphox.

Bulky Rain Sweeper.description:
• Archaludon is one of the main centerpieces of rain in Regulation M-A, capable of sweeping through entire teams while being exceptionally difficult to take down thanks to its immense physical bulk, Leftovers, Electro Shot, and Stamina. Electro Shot and Archaludon's typing give it a good matchup against Aerodactyl, Rotom-Wash, Talonflame, Mega Gengar, and Mega Blastoise.

  • Electro Shot: Electro Shot is Archaludon's main way of setting up while threatening common Pokemon like Basculegion-M, Pelipper, and Aerodactyl.

  • Positioning with Archaludon: Archaludon can switch into weaker attacks such as Aerodactyl's Dual Wingbeat and Fake Out from Sneasler and Incineroar to accumulate Stamina boosts. Archaludon should stay on the field as long as possible, as each Stamina boost makes it harder to take down.

Other Options

  • Draco Meteor: Draco Meteor can be used in place of Dragon Pulse to give Archaludon access to more firepower. This allows Archaludon to OHKO bulky Garchomp.

  • Aura Sphere: Aura Sphere is used to check opposing Kingambit, with a 50% chance to OHKO it. At +2, Archaludon also OHKOes Mega Tyranitar in sand with Aura Sphere.

Items

  • Leftovers: Leftovers grants Archaludon more longevity, enabling it to clean up games more easily.

Abilities

  • Stamina: Stamina allows Archaludon to become nigh impossible to KO with physical attacks, letting it tank several Earthquakes from Adamant Garchomp and Low Kicks from Kingambit.

SP Spreads

  • 32 HP / 1 Def / 5 SpA / 25 SpD / 3 Spe with Modest: This SP spread allows Archaludon to outspeed Choice Scarf Basculegion in Tailwind and survive Jolly Sneasler's Close Combat. The remaining points are put into Special Attack and Special Defense to maximize Archaludon's damage output and special bulk.

Teambuilding

  • Checks and Weaknesses: Archaludon's main weakness is its rather lackluster Special Defense, leaving it vulnerable to moves such as Mega Charizard Y's Weather Ball, Sylveon's Hyper Beam, and Mega Dragonite's Draco Meteor. Despite Archaludon's great physical bulk, Sneasler can threaten to OHKO it with Close Combat. Archaludon is extremely exploitable without any Stamina boosts, and its reliance on rain can make it tough to use in weather wars against Mega Charizard Y.

  • Good Partners and Synergies: Archaludon is typically found on rain teams along with Pelipper, Politoed, Sinistcha, and Basculegion-M. Pelipper and Politoed provide Archaludon with rain so it can set up with Electro Shot freely. Politoed is naturally bulkier and faster, whereas Pelipper has access to a Flying-type STAB move in Hurricane to threaten opposing Grass- and Fighting-types such as Sinistcha and Kommo-o. Pelipper also has access to supporting moves like Wide Guard to block moves such as Mega Charizard Y's Heat Wave and Mega Floette's Dazzling Gleam and Tailwind to allow Archaludon to outspeed Mega Aerodactyl and Choice Scarf Basculegion. Basculegion-M covers for Archaludon's weaknesses well, acting as a switch-in to Fighting-type moves such as Sneasler's Close Combat while threatening to OHKO most Garchomp with rain- and Adaptability-boosted Wave Crash. Basculegion-M also has the potential to OHKO frailer Mega Charizard Y through sun with Adaptability-boosted Wave Crash. Calm Mind Baton Pass Espathra can be utilized on rain compositions to give Archaludon an alternative way of setting up without being forced to use Electro Shot. Mega Dragonite acts as an alternative Tailwind setter for Archaludon while threatening to OHKO Sinistcha with Hurricane, preventing Sinistcha from using Life Dew or Trick Room. Sinistcha gives Archaludon maximum support through Life Dew and Hospitality recovery, Rage Powder redirection, and Trick Room speed control. Sableye gives Archaludon more bulk via dual screens while using moves such as Rain Dance, Encore, Disable, and Will-O-Wisp to disrupt foes. Rain Dance is used in weather wars, Encore can lock foes like Sneasler into Fake Out and Pokemon that may threaten Archaludon into Protect, Disable can prevent attacks such as Sneasler's Close Combat from threatening Archaludon and can force Choice Scarf users to use Struggle, and Will-O-Wisp can harm physical attackers.

  • How to Overcome Archaludon's Weaknesses: Archaludon's weakness to Sneasler's and Kommo-o's Fighting-type STAB moves can be patched up by threatening these Fighting-types with Pelipper's Hurricane, redirecting attacks with Sinistcha's Rage Powder, or switching Basculegion-M or Sinistcha into Sneasler's Close Combat and Kommo-o's Aura Sphere. Basculegion-M can heavily damage Garchomp with Adaptability-boosted Wave Crash or Last Respects after two or three allies have fainted. Archaludon's mediocre Special Defense can be patched up with Sableye's Light Screen and Special Defense boosts from Espathra's Calm Mind. Archaludon needs rain to set up with Electro Shot; therefore, having a manual Rain Dance user like Sableye alongside setters like Pelipper is great for keeping weather control when facing Mega Charizard Y.
